# Brain + Graph v1 readiness

## Context

Three streams of evidence converged this week:

1. **A user install report (Joseph)** — distill stalled at 75/237; `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` never
   appeared at repo level; doc ambiguity about where to run setup.
2. **Seven issues filed 2026-10-02** by two external testers (leine4550, peyton-alt).
3. **Two full agent transcripts** (Claude Code and Codex, same prompts, same repo) showing agents
   not using Brain or Graph.

Investigation of all three found that the headline problem is **not** that agents are habitual.
Three distinct, verified causes sit underneath it, and all are fixable.

**Already fixed and merged:** #316 (semantic memo on the wrong path, unbounded, unlinearized),
#317 (ollama envelope cap measuring the prompt, silent truncation, probe on an exhausted budget,
usage-accounting bypass, misleading flag help). **Open and green:** #306, #318, #320, #321.

This plan covers what is *not* taken care of.

---

## The three root causes

### 1. Brain's guide instructs agents to skip the tools

`internal/agentsetup/files.go:1-3` claims the package is "mirrored byte-for-byte in both
repositories". It is not. entire-graph carries directive text; entire-brain still carries a
permissive regression from 2026-09-14.

| entire-graph `guide.go:78-81` | entire-brain `guide.go:8-9`, `:31`, `:68` |
|---|---|
| "Your FIRST action … **MUST** be ONE Graph query" | "**Directly inspect source** when the task already provides sufficient locations" |
| "Do not skip the query on the grounds that the available context feels sufficient" | "**Skip ceremonial queries** for small edits and follow-up work" |
| | "Useful locations from the brief do not require a redundant Graph query" |

Claude's own transcript: *"The agent guide says to start substantive tasks with `entire brain
brief` and use Graph for code discovery. I skipped that."* It was following the guide it was given.

**`internal/agentsetup/coordination_test.go:137` and `scripts/test-agent-coordination.py:69`
actively ban the strings `"FIRST action"` and `"SEARCH FIRST"`** — and the same test *requires*
`"sufficient locations"` to be present. The permissive wording is enforced by CI in both
directions. Verified directly, not taken from a report.

**Graph has already diagnosed and fixed this.** Its `coordination_test.go:142-145` says:

> *"'FIRST action' and 'SEARCH FIRST' used to be banned here alongside those probes. They are not
> probes; they are the directive that makes the product get used, and **banning them was benchmark
> arm-fairness doctrine applied to shipped text.**"*

That is the root cause, and it is a good mistake: arm-fairness is correct for benchmarks — you
cannot give one arm instructions the other lacks — and was then applied to the guide that ships to
users, where there is no other arm. Graph's `guide.go:8` now reads "TWO KINDS OF WORDING LIVE IN
THIS PACKAGE, AND THEY MUST NOT BE UNIFIED", and it added `TestNormalGuideStaysDirective`.

So PR 3 is not reversing a deliberate product decision. It is **porting a fix graph already made
and documented**, for a cause graph already named. Brain never caught up.

Graph's guide (`guide.go:9-27`) states the measured cost: *"332 graph calls against 96,987
exploration calls (0.34%), and the graph-first rate was 0 in every session sampled."*

### 2. The tools punish the agent that does comply

From the Claude transcript, when finally instructed to run them:

| tool | result |
|---|---|
| `brain_status` | Error: 124,295 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_brief` | Error: 125,822 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_impact` | Error: 61,580 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_entity_history` | `"matches": []` |
| `brain_regressions` | `"no code identifiers found"`, `scanned_files: 0` |

A context-saving tool that overflows context is worse than no tool. `mcp_response_budget.go:54`
exists but is only a byte-budget *notice*.

### 3. Warnings and failures are silently dropped

A sweep found four HIGH instances of the class that has already cost this project repeatedly.
Worst: `internal/cli/semantic.go:2380` — `FilterWarnings` drops any warning whose Detail merely
*contains* a `.brainignore` pattern, by substring with no path parse. This repo's `.brainignore`
line 1 is `entire-brain`, a substring of every absolute path in it, so **every index warning is
discarded** and status reports a clean index that silently missed files.

### Also confirmed

- **Codex could not use Brain at all** — `entire` does not expose `brain`; it found the local
  executable by accident. Packaging/discovery gap, separate from compliance.
- **entire-graph ships no MCP server.** In an MCP-first harness the "MUST run a Graph query"
  instruction names a tool the agent does not have. 37 `brain_*` tools exist; **zero** tool
  descriptions mention grep, "first", "instead of" or "before".
- **`hook pre-edit` already exists** (`internal/cli/hook_cmd.go`, shipped in merged PR #24) and
  **nothing wires it**. Not in any settings template, not emitted by `init-agents`.
- The nested `entire-brain/` clone degrades Graph's index:
  `W_GIT_WORKTREE_FALLBACK: nested .git marker at "entire-brain/.git"`.

---

## Decisions, and why

**Three stacked PRs, not one.** PR1 and PR2 both touch `semantic.go` and `distill_cmd.go`, so they
genuinely conflict — stacking is correct here rather than cosmetic. Risk to accept: a stall in PR1
blocks 2 and 3. Mitigation: PR1 is the smallest and most obviously correct.

**Guide text before enforcement hook.** The guide currently says the opposite of what we want;
changing text is free and addresses the cause. The hook is belt-and-braces and goes in the same
PR, but we measure the guide change on its own first so we learn which one worked.

**Port graph's fix rather than invent one.** I was ready to flag the directive-wording ban as
needing the author's sign-off. Checking graph first showed it had already diagnosed the cause
(arm-fairness doctrine applied to shipped text), fixed it, and left both the reasoning and a
guard test behind. Copying a documented in-house fix beats re-deciding it.

**Not in scope, recommended separately:** an MCP server for entire-graph. It is the structural
reason the Graph instruction is unenforceable in Claude Code, but it is a build, not a fix.

---

## PR 1 — Retrieval returns usable output and reports what it dropped

Bottom of the stack. Nothing above matters if the tools error or lie.

**MCP response budget**
- `internal/cli/mcp.go`, `internal/cli/mcp_response_budget.go` — enforce a real byte/token ceiling
  on every `brain_*` response, not a notice. Truncate with an explicit, machine-readable marker
  naming what was dropped and how to get it (`--json`, a path, a narrower query).
- Worst offenders to verify: `brain_status`, `brain_brief`, `brain_impact`.

**Status latency (#325)**
- `internal/cli/verify_cmd.go:833` → `:424`, `internal/cli/agent_surface.go:1053` —
  `populateBrainStatusVerification` runs `git for-each-ref --contains <commit>` per distinct anchor
  commit, a full reachability walk. Gate verification behind `--details`; keep the summary cheap.

**The four HIGH silent-failure sites**
- `semantic.go:2380`/`:2518` — `FilterWarnings` substring match against `.brainignore`. Parse paths;
  never match on Detail text. Report a dropped-count.
- `regression.go:316`/`:1224` — `SkipAll` at 20000 scanned / 400 seen with no warning, then prints
  "No suspected regressions (scanned N files)". Emit a cap warning; correct the claim.
- `export.go:3588`,`:3619`/`:382` — `usefulExportWarnings` drops `checkpoint snapshot unavailable:`
  unless `--debug`, and the reported `warnings: %d` counts the filtered set.
- `distill_cmd.go:79` `capWarnings` — cap of 50 applied *before* persisting to the manifest, so the
  dropped text exists nowhere. Persist all; cap only the display.

**Truncated user-facing messages** (`status_render.go:264`, `statusCauseWidth=140`, byte-based)
- `semantic_stream.go:518` (182 chars), `semantic.go:1783` (173, still unfixed on main),
  `semantic.go:6720` (147). Shorten the strings; make truncation rune-aware.

## PR 2 — Multi-agent safety, indexing, and Windows

**#326 — `brain brief` takes `.git/index.lock`**
- `internal/cli/git_harden.go:78-81` is the single git spawn point and injects no
  `--no-optional-locks`. Add it there; swap `git diff --shortstat HEAD` → `diff-index`.
  Call sites: `semantic.go:2613`,`:2617`,`:5022`, `agent_surface.go:4768`.

**#327 — indexing stalls on a dirty worktree**
- `semantic.go:575` + `refresh.go:795-796`: dirty && !`--worktree` → `dirty_worktree` error, and
  needs-rebuild returns true unconditionally on dirty, so every refresh hits the refusal.
  `watch.go:305-309` aborts the whole tick, so the cursor never advances. Index HEAD via a temp
  tree; let watch skip only the semantic step. Same shape at `seed.go:276`.

**#328 — Ollama is loopback-only and never auto-selected**
- `refresh.go:829-840` `defaultRefreshAgent` tries codex→claude→none with ollama absent;
  `distill_cmd.go:2349` rejects a non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL` **silently**;
  `watch.go:110` hardcodes `"codex"`; `embed.go:300` repeats the pattern.
  Add an opt-in remote host, add ollama to the auto order, and **warn loudly when a configured URL
  is ignored** — silent fallback to a cloud agent is the privacy bug in the report.

**#322 — Windows "command line is too long"**
- `distill.go:137`, exec at `distill_cmd.go:2237`: argv ends `"--system-prompt", <7516-byte
  prompt>`, blowing cmd.exe's 8191 limit. The chunk is already on stdin. Move the prompt to stdin
  or a temp file. ~15 callers share `distillAgentCommandArgs` (`seed.go:1830`, `facts_eval`,
  `facts_write_cmd`, `pattern_*`) — fix at the shared builder.
- **Verification limit, stated up front:** I cannot run Windows here. The test asserts the prompt
  is not on argv and that total argv stays under 8191, which is deterministic on any platform.

**#324 — `facts promote --keep-both` queues confidence-0 proposals**
- `internal/factmerge/admin.go:128` emits `Proposal{Action: ActionSupersede, Confidence: 0}` as a
  literal, with no similarity ever computed, once per same-path target — quadratic fanout.
  Compute similarity, or do not queue when confidence is 0. Callers: `factsync/sync.go:118`,
  `facts_sync_cmd.go`, `facts_admin_cmd.go`.

## PR 3 — The guide, the hook, and discovery

**Restore directive wording in brain's guide — port graph's fix**
- `internal/agentsetup/guide.go:8-9`,`:31`,`:68`,`:11-12` — align with entire-graph's text,
  including its `guide.go:8` header comment explaining why the two wordings must not be unified.
- `coordination_test.go:137` — remove `"FIRST action"`/`"SEARCH FIRST"` from the `bad` list and
  `"sufficient locations"` from the `want` list, keeping the genuine runtime-probe bans
  (`entire plugin list`, `command -v`, `setup.json`). Carry over graph's explanatory comment.
- Add brain's equivalent of `TestNormalGuideStaysDirective` so the regression cannot recur.
- `scripts/test-agent-coordination.py:69` — same ban, same change.

**#323 — the guide names a command that does not exist**
- `guide.go:33`,`:74`, `strict.go:66` hardcode `entire graph query`; entire-graph v0.4.0 dispatch
  has only `case "search"` (`query` lands in unreleased 0.5.0). Emit `search`, or probe
  `graph capabilities --json`. Same stale text at `docs/agent-coordination.md:107`.

**Wire the hook that already exists**
- `internal/cli/hook_cmd.go` (`hook pre-edit`, `hook post-failure`) is registered hidden at
  `root.go:169` and wired nowhere. Emit the `PreToolUse` wiring from `init-agents` so it lands in
  `.claude/settings.json` alongside the guide. Existing `PreToolUse` entries use
  `"matcher": "Agent"` only; this needs a Bash/Grep/Read matcher.

**MCP tool descriptions**
- `mcp.go:805-1030`, 37 tools. None say when to use the tool *instead of* grep. The description is
  what an agent reads when choosing; the guide is a file it may never open.

**In-repo docs**
- `README.md` — move the "What to ask" table (currently line 124 of 362) near the top and drop the
  Brain-command column, per Joseph's feedback. Fix its `query`→`recall` verbs for decision
  questions.
- `docs/agent-coordination.md:107` — stale `entire graph query`.

---

## Docs that are NOT in this repo

These live on the docs site, so they cannot be part of these PRs. They ship as a change list plus
an artifact (below), for whoever owns the site.

| Page | Fix |
|---|---|
| Continuous Agent Memory | **"up to 71%" is a retracted figure** — that instance had the graph arm silently falling back to grep on a zero-byte payload and a 452-word stripped baseline. Replace with cost +2.49% (CI [−6.83, +11.18]) or drop the number. |
| Continuous Agent Memory | `entire/agent-guide.md` → `.entire/agent-guide.md` (leading dot) |
| Continuous Agent Memory | `entire graph stats --repo` errors without a value — drop the flag |
| Continuous Agent Memory | Remove the `entire graph stats` recommendation (reported 82.9M saved vs an honest ~46k) |
| Continuous Agent Memory | The rerun instruction is prose; make it a code block |
| Overview | **Add `entire brain init-agents` to the setup section** — `setup` never writes AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, which is why Joseph saw nothing even from the repo root |
| Overview | "From your repository's root" → "…not from a cloned `entire-brain` directory" |
| Overview | `query` → `recall` for the decision example; document that facts are branch-scoped |
| Overview + Use Cases | Copy fixes: "For example,you can move"; "lessons that **has**"; the run-on "…and make sure to commit…" |
| Use Cases | `inspect impact --symbol X` **errors** (`unknown flag: --symbol`) — it is positional |
| All | Confirm the "CLI 0.10.0 or later" floor; no version gate exists in brain's source |

**Deliverable:** a two-tab artifact — tab 1 every problem with evidence and severity, tab 2 the
corrected pages as they should read.

---

## Verification

Each fix gets a reproduction that fails before and passes after. Mutation-verified: patch the
guard, prove the test goes red (`verified-by-weakening`).

| Fix | Reproduction |
|---|---|
| MCP budget | Call `brain_status`/`brain_brief`/`brain_impact` against a large repo; assert every response is under the cap and carries a dropped-marker |
| #325 | Brain with ~250 facts; assert `status --json` under a wall-clock threshold; assert `--details` still verifies |
| FilterWarnings | `.brainignore` containing a string that is a substring of an absolute path; assert warnings survive |
| regression cap | Corpus over 20000 files; assert a cap warning appears and the "no regressions" claim is qualified |
| export/capWarnings | Assert dropped warnings are persisted and recoverable |
| #326 | Hold a `brain brief` while running `git status` concurrently; assert no lock error. Deterministic form: assert `--no-optional-locks` in the spawn args |
| #327 | Dirty worktree + commit + refresh; assert the index advances rather than refusing |
| #328 | Non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL`; assert a loud warning, and that opt-in remote works |
| #322 | Assert the prompt is not on argv and total argv < 8191 (platform-independent) |
| #324 | `promote --keep-both` over same-path facts; assert no confidence-0 proposals and no quadratic fanout |
| Guide | Assert the generated guide contains the directive sentence and names only commands the installed graph exposes |

**Loop:** run the full `internal/...` suite under `-race` (CI runs `-race`; local darwin does not),
re-run each reproduction, repeat until two consecutive passes find nothing new. One suite at a
time — concurrent runs contend over the global brain data dir and produce false failures.

### The usage experiment (the deeper ask)

`entire graph stats` already computes a **graph-first rate**, and graph's guide records the
baseline: 0.34% of calls, graph-first rate 0 in every session sampled.

1. Measure the baseline on a repo with the current permissive guide.
2. Install the corrected guide. Run a fleet of subagents on real tasks (locate, impact, "why did
   we"), each in its own worktree.
3. Re-measure graph-first rate.
4. Then enable the hook and measure again — so we learn whether wording alone was enough.
5. Collect each agent's own account of why it did or did not reach for the tool. That self-report
   is what exposed cause #1; it is the highest-yield signal we have.

---

## Sequencing

1. PR 1 — retrieval correctness (smallest, most obviously right, unblocks the stack)
2. PR 2 — multi-agent safety, indexing, Windows
3. PR 3 — guide, hook, discovery, in-repo docs
4. Docs artifact for the off-repo pages
5. Usage experiment, reported with before/after graph-first rate

Nothing merges without approval.

## Recommended, but not in these PRs

**An MCP server for entire-graph.** Brain ships 37 `brain_*` MCP tools; graph ships none. In
Claude Code the guide's "MUST run a Graph query" names a tool the agent does not have, so the
directive is unenforceable in the harness most users are in. This is the structural half of the
usage problem and the guide fix will only partly land without it. It is a build, not a fix, and
wants its own decision.

**Deferred with reasons, say the word to include:** nothing — all seven filed issues are in scope.
The only stated verification limit is #322, which cannot be executed on macOS; its test is
platform-independent but a real Windows run should confirm before closing the issue.

**#328 — Ollama is loopback-only and never auto-selected**
- `refresh.go:829-840` `defaultRefreshAgent` tries codex→claude→none with ollama absent;
  `distill_cmd.go:2349` rejects a non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL` **silently**;
  `watch.go:110` hardcodes `"codex"`; `embed.go:300` repeats the pattern.
  Add an opt-in remote host, add ollama to the auto order, and **warn loudly when a configured URL
  is ignored** — silent fallback to a cloud agent is the privacy bug in the report.

**#322 — Windows "command line is too long"**
- `distill.go:137`, exec at `distill_cmd.go:2237`: argv ends `"--system-prompt", <7516-byte
  prompt>`, blowing cmd.exe's 8191 limit. The chunk is already on stdin. Move the prompt to stdin
  or a temp file. ~15 callers share `distillAgentCommandArgs` (`seed.go:1830`, `facts_eval`,
  `facts_write_cmd`, `pattern_*`) — fix at the shared builder.
- **Verification limit, stated up front:** I cannot run Windows here. The test asserts the prompt
  is not on argv and that total argv stays under 8191, which is deterministic on any platform.

**#324 — `facts promote --keep-both` queues confidence-0 proposals**
- `internal/factmerge/admin.go:128` emits `Proposal{Action: ActionSupersede, Confidence: 0}` as a
  literal, with no similarity ever computed, once per same-path target — quadratic fanout.
  Compute similarity, or do not queue when confidence is 0. Callers: `factsync/sync.go:118`,
  `facts_sync_cmd.go`, `facts_admin_cmd.go`.

## PR 3 — The guide, the hook, and discovery

**Restore directive wording in brain's guide — port graph's fix**
- `internal/agentsetup/guide.go:8-9`,`:31`,`:68`,`:11-12` — align with entire-graph's text,
  including its `guide.go:8` header comment explaining why the two wordings must not be unified.
- `coordination_test.go:137` — remove `"FIRST action"`/`"SEARCH FIRST"` from the `bad` list and
  `"sufficient locations"` from the `want` list, keeping the genuine runtime-probe bans
  (`entire plugin list`, `command -v`, `setup.json`). Carry over graph's explanatory comment.
- Add brain's equivalent of `TestNormalGuideStaysDirective` so the regression cannot recur.
- `scripts/test-agent-coordination.py:69` — same ban, same change.

**#323 — the guide names a command that does not exist**
- `guide.go:33`,`:74`, `strict.go:66` hardcode `entire graph query`; entire-graph v0.4.0 dispatch
  has only `case "search"` (`query` lands in unreleased 0.5.0). Emit `search`, or probe
  `graph capabilities --json`. Same stale text at `docs/agent-coordination.md:107`.

**Wire the hook that already exists**
- `internal/cli/hook_cmd.go` (`hook pre-edit`, `hook post-failure`) is registered hidden at
  `root.go:169` and wired nowhere. Emit the `PreToolUse` wiring from `init-agents` so it lands in
  `.claude/settings.json` alongside the guide. Existing `PreToolUse` entries use
  `"matcher": "Agent"` only; this needs a Bash/Grep/Read matcher.

**MCP tool descriptions**
- `mcp.go:805-1030`, 37 tools. None say when to use the tool *instead of* grep. The description is
  what an agent reads when choosing; the guide is a file it may never open.

**In-repo docs**
- `README.md` — move the "What to ask" table (currently line 124 of 362) near the top and drop the
  Brain-command column, per Joseph's feedback. Fix its `query`→`recall` verbs for decision
  questions.
- `docs/agent-coordination.md:107` — stale `entire graph query`.

---

## Docs that are NOT in this repo

These live on the docs site, so they cannot be part of these PRs. They ship as a change list plus
an artifact (below), for whoever owns the site.

| Page | Fix |
|---|---|
| Continuous Agent Memory | **"up to 71%" is a retracted figure** — that instance had the graph arm silently falling back to grep on a zero-byte payload and a 452-word stripped baseline. Replace with cost +2.49% (CI [−6.83, +11.18]) or drop the number. |
| Continuous Agent Memory | `entire/agent-guide.md` → `.entire/agent-guide.md` (leading dot) |
| Continuous Agent Memory | `entire graph stats --repo` errors without a value — drop the flag |
| Continuous Agent Memory | Remove the `entire graph stats` recommendation (reported 82.9M saved vs an honest ~46k) |
| Continuous Agent Memory | The rerun instruction is prose; make it a code block |
| Overview | **Add `entire brain init-agents` to the setup section** — `setup` never writes AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, which is why Joseph saw nothing even from the repo root |
| Overview | "From your repository's root" → "…not from a cloned `entire-brain` directory" |
| Overview | `query` → `recall` for the decision example; document that facts are branch-scoped |
| Overview + Use Cases | Copy fixes: "For example,you can move"; "lessons that **has**"; the run-on "…and make sure to commit…" |
| Use Cases | `inspect impact --symbol X` **errors** (`unknown flag: --symbol`) — it is positional |
| All | Confirm the "CLI 0.10.0 or later" floor; no version gate exists in brain's source |

**Deliverable:** a two-tab artifact — tab 1 every problem with evidence and severity, tab 2 the
corrected pages as they should read.

---

## Verification

Each fix gets a reproduction that fails before and passes after. Mutation-verified: patch the
guard, prove the test goes red (`verified-by-weakening`).

| Fix | Reproduction |
|---|---|
| MCP budget | Call `brain_status`/`brain_brief`/`brain_impact` against a large repo; assert every response is under the cap and carries a dropped-marker |
| #325 | Brain with ~250 facts; assert `status --json` under a wall-clock threshold; assert `--details` still verifies |
| FilterWarnings | `.brainignore` containing a string that is a substring of an absolute path; assert warnings survive |
| regression cap | Corpus over 20000 files; assert a cap warning appears and the "no regressions" claim is qualified |
| export/capWarnings | Assert dropped warnings are persisted and recoverable |
| #326 | Hold a `brain brief` while running `git status` concurrently; assert no lock error. Deterministic form: assert `--no-optional-locks` in the spawn args |
| #327 | Dirty worktree + commit + refresh; assert the index advances rather than refusing |
| #328 | Non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL`; assert a loud warning, and that opt-in remote works |
| #322 | Assert the prompt is not on argv and total argv < 8191 (platform-independent) |
| #324 | `promote --keep-both` over same-path facts; assert no confidence-0 proposals and no quadratic fanout |
| Guide | Assert the generated guide contains the directive sentence and names only commands the installed graph exposes |

**Loop:** run the full `internal/...` suite under `-race` (CI runs `-race`; local darwin does not),
re-run each reproduction, repeat until two consecutive passes find nothing new. One suite at a
time — concurrent runs contend over the global brain data dir and produce false failures.

### The usage experiment (the deeper ask)

`entire graph stats` already computes a **graph-first rate**, and graph's guide records the
baseline: 0.34% of calls, graph-first rate 0 in every session sampled.

1. Measure the baseline on a repo with the current permissive guide.
2. Install the corrected guide. Run a fleet of subagents on real tasks (locate, impact, "why did
   we"), each in its own worktree.
3. Re-measure graph-first rate.
4. Then enable the hook and measure again — so we learn whether wording alone was enough.
5. Collect each agent's own account of why it did or did not reach for the tool. That self-report
   is what exposed cause #1; it is the highest-yield signal we have.

---

## Sequencing

1. PR 1 — retrieval correctness (smallest, most obviously right, unblocks the stack)
2. PR 2 — multi-agent safety, indexing, Windows
3. PR 3 — guide, hook, discovery, in-repo docs
4. Docs artifact for the off-repo pages
5. Usage experiment, reported with before/after graph-first rate

Nothing merges without approval.

## Recommended, but not in these PRs

**An MCP server for entire-graph.** Brain ships 37 `brain_*` MCP tools; graph ships none. In
Claude Code the guide's "MUST run a Graph query" names a tool the agent does not have, so the
directive is unenforceable in the harness most users are in. This is the structural half of the
usage problem and the guide fix will only partly land without it. It is a build, not a fix, and
wants its own decision.

**Deferred with reasons, say the word to include:** nothing — all seven filed issues are in scope.
The only stated verification limit is #322, which cannot be executed on macOS; its test is
platform-independent but a real Windows run should confirm before closing the issue.

FIX issue #325: `entire brain status --json` takes ~1 minute once facts exist (reported: 51 sessions, 253 facts). It was fast at 0 facts, which rules it out for hooks — and our own docs suggest wiring status into hooks.

ROOT CAUSE, already located, verify it yourself before changing anything:

- Per distinct anchor commit it runs `git cat-file -e` AND `git for-each-ref --contains <commit> refs/heads refs/remotes refs/tags` — a full reachability walk, cached per-commit only.
- Cost scales with refs x history x distinct anchor commits, NOT linearly with fact count.

REQUIRED: make the default `status`/`status --json` cheap. Gate the verification work behind an explicit opt-in (e.g. `--details`, or whatever flag already exists — check first, reuse rather than invent). `brain verify` must keep its current full behaviour. \t// against the original 128 KiB budget. It is not a free-standing number: it
\t// is a number of rows that fitted in THAT budget, so it has to move with the

\tmcpResponseTrimFairRowsAt128K = 64

\tmcpResponseTrimFairRowsFloor  = 8

s += '''
// mcpResponseTrimFairRows scales the per-list row guarantee with the active
// budget, holding the original calibration exactly at the budget it was tuned

// A floor keeps the guarantee meaningful: below a handful of rows per list the

content.text: Two things wrong: a meta-notice doesn't belong in `PartialFailures` at all, and its wording ("provider warning(s)") is false when it's filtering failures. The disclosure should be one accurate notice, in the list where "something you should know" belongs:

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-v1-retrieval
python3 - <<'PY'
p='internal/cli/semantic.go'; s=open(p).read()
anchor='func (i brainIgnore) FilterWarningsReported(warnings []semanticWarning) []semanticWarning {'
assert s.count(anchor)==1
add = '''// filterIgnoredWarningLists filters a header's two warning lists together and
// discloses, in the warnings list only, how much each one lost.
//
// Disclosure has to live in exactly one place and be accurate about what it
// covers. Appending a notice to each list separately put "N provider
// warning(s) were withheld" inside PartialFailures, where it is wrong twice
// over: a withheld-count notice is not a partial failure, and the entries it
// was counting there were failures, not warnings. Partial failures being
// hidden is the more serious of the two, so it is named explicitly rather than
// folded into one total.
func (i brainIgnore) filterIgnoredWarningLists(warnings, partialFailures []semanticWarning) ([]semanticWarning, []semanticWarning) {
	keptWarnings, droppedWarnings := i.filterWarningsCounted(warnings)
	keptFailures, droppedFailures := i.filterWarningsCounted(partialFailures)
	if droppedWarnings+droppedFailures == 0 {
		return keptWarnings, keptFailures
	}

	var detail string
	switch {
	case droppedFailures == 0:
		detail = fmt.Sprintf("%d provider warning(s) named ignored paths and were withheld by brainignore rules", droppedWarnings)
	case droppedWarnings == 0:
		detail = fmt.Sprintf("%d partial indexing failure(s) named ignored paths and were withheld by brainignore rules", droppedFailures)
	default:
		detail = fmt.Sprintf("%d provider warning(s) and %d partial indexing failure(s) named ignored paths and were withheld by brainignore rules",
			droppedWarnings, droppedFailures)
	}
	// The notice carries no path token of its own, so re-filtering an already
	// filtered snapshot cannot swallow it.
	return append(keptWarnings, semanticWarning{
		Code:     warningsHiddenCode,
		Severity: "warning",
		Effect:   "this warning list is incomplete",
		Detail:   detail,
	}), keptFailures
}

'''
s = s.replace(anchor, add+anchor, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s); print("paired filter added")
PY

**PR 1 is open: [entire-brain#329](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/329)** — not merging without your approval.

## The headline finding

My own plan was wrong about the central bug, and correcting it made the fix sharper. The MCP trimming machinery was never broken — all three failing responses were **under** brain's budget and worked exactly as designed. The budget was sized against the **4 MiB transport frame** instead of against the agent's context window. 128 KiB of this JSON is ~52k tokens, double what a client reserves for one tool result.

Now 32 KiB, overridable. And the 64-row fair-share constant turned out to be calibrated to that same 128 KiB — leaving it fixed made every list collapse to one shared width, so it had to scale too.

- The budget was required to **equal** the retrieval budget — that coupling is how 128 KiB got there, since a terminal has no token limit. Now a ceiling.

**PR 1 merged into the stack and PR 3's core is done.** Here's the state:

## PR 3 — the root cause, fixed

The guide was telling agents *not* to use the tools, and **CI enforced it from both directions**: the test banned the directive strings `"FIRST action"`/`"SEARCH FIRST"` *and* required `"sufficient locations"` to be present.

I found it pinned in **three** places, not the two the plan listed — `coordination_test.go`, `scripts/test-agent-coordination.py`, and `strict_test.go:55`, which asserted normal mode *contains* `"Skip ceremonial queries"`.

Two things I didn't expect:

- **`combinedWorkflow` carried no Graph obligation at all.** It was `brainWorkflow` plus a capability list. That's the guide most users get, so an agent reading it had nothing telling it to check the call graph before editing.
- **The command in the guide doesn't exist** (#323). The installed binary here is a symlink to the dev checkout at v0.4.1-nightly, where `query` works — the stale-binary trap. I tested `search` against the same build: it works there *and* is the only verb in released 0.4.0. So `search` is correct against every graph a user might have.

## The hook

`hook pre-edit` has shipped since PR #24 with nothing invoking it. Wiring it turned up a scoping problem the plan missed: **brain doesn't write `.claude/settings.json` — `entire enable` does.** So it merges rather than writes: unrelated keys preserved, other products' entries untouched, idempotent by command match, and it *refuses and reports* on anything it doesn't recognise rather than overwriting. Tests cover all four, each weakening-verified.

I also used the existing `Edit|Write|MultiEdit` matcher rather than `Agent` — the entries `entire enable` writes use `Agent` only, which never fires at the moment a fact about the file would change the edit.

doc, or a comment someone sent you from one, is about that document, which

made from it): create the artifact from the type — `type_url` = the type's
link, `title` = the doc's title as its reader would say it ("Q3 hiring

from.content:
## How this was checked

Every command on both pages was executed against a real indexed brain in the `entire-brain` repository, on `entire-graph v0.4.1-nightly`. Nothing below is inferred from reading source.

One caution about the method, because it nearly produced a wrong report. My first pass wrapped each command in `timeout 60`. macOS ships no `timeout` binary, so every command failed with `command not found`, which did not match the error pattern I was grepping for — and all ten commands were recorded as passing. The three failures on this page only appeared after I removed the wrapper and checked exit codes directly. A verification harness that cannot fail is worse than no harness.

## Broken commands

These three do not work. A reader who copies them gets an error, which teaches them the tool is broken rather than that the page is wrong.

| Page | Documented | Error | Correct |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Use Cases | `entire brain inspect impact --symbol X` | `unknown flag: --symbol` | `entire brain inspect impact X` (positional) |
| Use Cases | `entire brain query --keyword "rate limiter"` | `unknown flag: --keyword` | `entire brain search "rate limiter"` |
| Use Cases | `entire brain query --semantic "..."` | `unknown flag: --semantic` | `entire brain vsearch "..."` |

The last two are not flag renames. Keyword and vector search are separate verbs, and `query` is the hybrid of both:

- `search` — lexical keyword search (BM25)
- `vsearch` — vector search
- `query` — hybrid of the two, reciprocal-rank fused
- `recall` — durable facts for the current branch

The original page used one verb with two invented flags where four distinct verbs exist.

## Wrong or missing guidance

**The setup section omits the command that writes the agent files.** This is the most consequential item on the page. `entire brain setup` never writes `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` — only `entire brain init-agents` does, and the page never mentions it. A user who followed the page exactly reported that neither file appeared, and tried a second setup option believing he had run it from the wrong directory. He had not: the page simply omits the step. Add `entire brain init-agents` to the setup sequence.

**"From your repository's root" is ambiguous in the one case that bites.** If someone has cloned `entire-brain` itself to install it, its root is also a repository root. Brain walks up to the *nearest* `.git`, so running setup there indexes the wrong repository and silently succeeds. Say "your own project's root, not a cloned `entire-brain` directory".

**Facts are branch-scoped, and the page never says so.** Verified on one brain, two branches:

```
$ entire brain recall "retry policy"
no facts for "retry policy" on fix/agent-guide-directive-and-discovery

$ entire brain recall "warning" --branch main
fact:7583ec00faa9c828dfa23219 invariant [constraints.invariants.general]
```

The empty result reads as "nothing was ever recorded" when it means "nothing on this branch". One sentence and the `--branch` flag prevent that reading.

**The decision example uses the wrong verb.** For "why did we choose this retry policy" the page shows `query`, which searches prose across docs and history. Recorded decisions are facts, so `recall` is the verb — with the branch caveat above attached.

## Numbers that cannot be published

**"Up to 71%" is retracted.** It came from a single benchmark instance where the graph arm silently fell back to grep on a zero-byte payload while the baseline ran against a 452-word stripped prompt — one of only three empty-payload logs in 1,774 runs. It measures a harness bug, not the product.

The defensible figure from the same work is a cost delta of **+2.49%**, with a bootstrap confidence interval of [−6.83, +11.18] that crosses zero. That is an honest way of saying the effect is not distinguishable from noise at this sample size. Either publish it with the interval, or publish no number. A number with the interval removed is the same error in a smaller font.

**Remove the `entire graph stats` recommendation.** It reports cumulative savings against a counterfactual it cannot observe. On this repository it has reported 82.9M tokens saved where the paired benchmark supports roughly 46k — off by about 1,800x. A savings figure that disagrees with the controlled measurement is wrong, not impressive, and a user who quotes it will be contradicted.

**`entire graph stats --repo` errors as written** — the flag takes a value. Since the recommendation is being removed, the line goes with it.

## Copy and formatting

| Page | Written | Should be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overview | `entire/agent-guide.md` | `.entire/agent-guide.md` (leading dot) |
| Overview | "For example,you can move" | missing space after the comma |
| Use Cases | "lessons that has" | "lessons that have" |
| Use Cases | the rerun instruction set as prose | a code block, like every other command |
| Overview | "...and make sure to commit..." | split; the sentence runs on |

The `entire/agent-guide.md` path is not only a typo: without the dot it names a directory that does not exist, so a reader who goes looking finds nothing and concludes the file was never written.

## One open question

Both pages state a floor of "CLI 0.10.0 or later". I could not find any version gate for this in Brain's source — no check, no constant, no error path. Either the floor is enforced somewhere I did not look, or it is a figure carried over from an earlier document. Someone who knows should confirm it before it ships again; a version requirement that nothing enforces will drift silently.

You can use Brain to find earlier decisions, save lessons, and give your agent context before it starts work. Below are some ways to use Brain in your project.

[Install Brain and set up your repository](/guides/brain/overview#before-you-start) first. Run these commands from the repository, and replace the example questions and rules with your own.

## Get to Know a Project

If you are joining a project or returning after a break, you can ask Brain for an overview of its structure, tools, and conventions.

```bash
entire brain overview
```

## Get Context Before Starting a Task

Describe what you want to build or change. Brain gathers relevant facts, earlier work, code locations, and possible tests into a brief.

```bash
entire brain brief "add rate limiting to the upload endpoint"
```

You can now use the brief to plan your work or give your coding agent a starting point.

## Find Out Why a Decision Was Made

Search earlier work before reopening a decision or trying an approach your team has already explored.

```bash
entire brain query "why did we remove the queue abstraction"
```

This helps you read the supporting sources to understand the decision and whether it still applies.

## Search for a Topic

If you are searching for a topic and know the keyword, you can use it with the command below:

```bash
entire brain query --keyword "rate limiter"
```

And if you know the problem but not the exact words, you can search by meaning:

```bash
entire brain query --semantic "handling temporary request failures"
```

Without either flag, `query` combines keyword and meaning-based search. Make sure to use only one of these flags at a time.

## Save a Rule for Future Work

You can also record a decision or lesson so another session can find it. It is advisable to only save rules that are true for your project.

```bash
entire brain remember "Retry failed requests at most three times." --path constraints.retry.policy
```

The path flag groups the fact under a topic. This lets you save the fact without asking an agent to choose a category.

## Look Up Saved Rules

Before changing behavior, you can check what your project has already recorded about it.

```bash
entire brain recall "retry policy"
```

Use `recall` for saved facts and `query` for a broader search across facts, history, and docs.

## Check What a Code Change Could Affect

With Entire Graph installed, inspect the impact of changing a function or type. Replace `ValidateToken` with a symbol from your code.

```bash
entire brain inspect impact --symbol ValidateToken
```

You can also inspect changes since the last index:

```bash
entire brain inspect changes
```

## Check Whether Memory Is Current

You can see which sources are available, missing, or out of date, using:

```bash
entire brain status --verbose
```

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-v1-safety
git add -A
cat > ~/.local/state/entire-distill/pr2msg.txt <<'EOF'
fix(safety): stop brain colliding with concurrent git, stalling on a dirty tree, and ignoring local models

Five filed issues, all reproduced before being changed.

#326 - brain brief takes .git/index.lock
-----------------------------------------
Two agents in one repository is the normal case for this product, so a read-only
inspection that takes a write lock is a correctness bug.

`--no-optional-locks` is now injected at the single git spawn point, which closes
`git status`. It is NOT sufficient on its own: a porcelain `git diff <commit>`
performs its own index refresh that the optional-lock setting does not gate.
Measured on git 2.54.0, each trial from an identical stat-dirty index, restored
in between:

    git diff --name-status -M -C HEAD                      REWRITES the index
    git --no-optional-locks diff --name-status -M -C HEAD   REWRITES the index
    git --no-optional-locks diff-index --name-status ...    leaves it alone

That matters because changedSemanticFiles runs inside `brain brief` - the exact
command the issue reports.

Converting those diffs to plumbing would fix the lock and change the answer:
diff-index against an unrefreshed index reports a stat-dirty file (mtime
touched, content identical) as modified, which here means re-indexing a file
that did not change. On the same fixture that cost one spurious path.

So the worktree-vs-HEAD diffs now run with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointing at a COPY of
the index. git refreshes the copy, the real index is never opened for write, and
the output is byte-identical to porcelain because it IS porcelain. Verified: the
copy's output matched the real one exactly, where plumbing differed by one line.

One diff that exists purely to report a stat moved to `diff-index` as well.

#327 - indexing stalls on a dirty worktree
-------------------------------------------
A loop, not a single bug: a dirty tree forced a rebuild, the indexer REFUSED
that rebuild without --worktree, and a failed refresh aborted the whole watch
tick so the cursor never advanced. Nothing progressed for as long as the tree
stayed dirty, which for anyone working is most of the time.

Dirtiness alone says nothing about whether the INDEXED content is stale: the
index describes HEAD, and HEAD has not moved because the worktree has
uncommitted edits. The two cases where it does matter - a snapshot taken in
worktree mode, or from a dirty tree - were already decided further down, so the
check was redundant as well as harmful. A dirty-worktree refusal now lets the
watch tick continue; every other refresh failure still aborts it, because an
unrefreshed brain must not have tokens spent against it.

#328 - a local model is installed and never used
-------------------------------------------------
defaultRefreshAgent tried codex, then claude, then none. A user who installed
ollama specifically to keep transcripts off a third party got one of two
outcomes: no distillation at all, or - if a cloud CLI happened to be installed
too - their session content sent to that provider instead.

ollama is now tried FIRST. Transcripts are the most sensitive thing this product
touches; when a local model is available, using it is what the user configured.
This changes the agent for someone who has both installed. `--agent` still
overrides per run.

`watch` hardcoded codex, which is the same defect and worse: the watcher runs
unattended, so the transcripts went out on a timer. It now uses the "auto"
sentinel - note that "" is NOT that sentinel and passes through as an invalid
agent name.

The issue also reports that a non-loopback ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL is rejected

Third of three. Stacked on #330 — **base is `fix/multiagent-safety-indexing-windows`, not `main`.**

This is the root cause of "agents don't use Brain or Graph." It is not that agents are habitual.

## The guide told them not to, and CI enforced it both ways

`coordination_test.go` **banned** the directive strings `"FIRST action"` and `"SEARCH FIRST"`, and separately **required** `"sufficient locations"` to be present. The permissive wording was pinned from both directions at once.

It came from benchmark arm-fairness doctrine, which forbids giving one arm an instruction the other lacks. Correct for an A/B cell; fatal for shipped text — in a user's repo there is no second arm, only an agent deciding whether to bother. Measured afterwards: **332 graph calls against 96,987 exploration calls (0.34%)**, graph-first rate **0** in every session sampled.

A Claude session asked to explain itself said it had been told to start with `brain brief` and skipped it. It was following the guide it was given.

entire-graph diagnosed this, fixed its own copy, and left the reasoning and a guard behind. **This is that fix, ported** — not a new product decision — plus three things its port did not cover.

## Three things the port did not cover

**It was pinned in three places, not two.** `strict_test.go` asserted that *normal* mode contains `"Skip ceremonial queries"`. Normal mode is distinguished from strict by its mode, not by offering the agent a way out.

**`combinedWorkflow` carried no Graph obligation at all.** It was `brainWorkflow` plus a capability list — and it is the guide most users get. An agent reading it had nothing telling it to check the call graph before editing.

**#323 — the guide named a command that does not exist.** `entire graph query` is absent from the released v0.4.0 dispatch. The binary installed here is a symlink to a dev checkout where it *does* exist, which is how this survived review. `search` is the only verb correct against every graph a user may have: the sole verb in 0.4.0, still an alias on 0.4.1+. Verified against the running build.

## The hook that shipped and was never called

`hook pre-edit` has existed since PR #24 with **nothing invoking it** — the only push path in a product that is otherwise entirely pull, which is precisely the measured problem.

Wiring it surfaced a scoping issue: **brain does not own `.claude/settings.json`** — `entire enable` writes it. So it **merges**: unrelated keys preserved, other products' entries untouched, idempotent by command match, and it *refuses and reports* on anything it does not recognise rather than overwriting. Matcher is `Edit|Write|MultiEdit`, not the `Agent`-only matcher `entire enable` writes, which never fires at the moment a fact about the file would change the edit.

## Tool descriptions and README

37 `brain_*` tools, **none** of which said when to use the tool instead of grep. The description is what an agent reads when choosing; the guide is a file it may never open. 23 rewritten with a substitution cue and a limit. The test iterates the live tool table with an explicit deny-list, so a new tool fails by default.

Two byte-budget pins moved (917→1090, 1167→1263) with the reasoning recorded in place: this is sent once per session in the tool list, not per call.

README: the "What to ask" table moved from line 124 to the top, command column dropped, verbs corrected against commands actually run, and branch-scoped facts stated.

`TestNormalGuideStaysDirective` pins the absence of every exit **by its exact words** and the presence of the directive. `TestGuidesNameOnlyCommandsGraphExposes` pins #323. Both verified by weakening, along with the four hook-merge guards.

Full `./...` green under `-race` across the whole stack; lint clean.

Not merging without your approval.

input.content:
---
name: verification-harness-false-pass
description: My own verification commands silently no-opped three times in one session, each producing a comfortable false PASS, never a false failure
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A check that cannot fail reports success. This happened three times in one
session, by three different mechanisms, and every time the bogus answer was the
one that let me stop looking:

1. **`timeout` does not exist on macOS.** `timeout 60 <cmd>` failed with
   "command not found", which did not match the error pattern I was grepping
   for, so ten broken doc commands were recorded as `ok`. Three of them were
   genuinely broken.
2. **`.git` is a FILE in a worktree, not a directory.** `md5sum .git/index`
   failed identically before and after, the hashes "matched", and I reported a
   subagent's correct measurement as wrong.
3. **Trials that mutate the thing they measure.** Running `git diff` to test
   whether it refreshes the index refreshes the index, so trial 2 saw a clean
   state and passed. Only snapshot-restore between trials gave a stable answer.

**Why:** a false failure is loud and gets investigated; a false pass is silent
and ends the investigation. The asymmetry means an unreliable harness
systematically moves me toward "no problem here".

**How to apply:** before trusting any verification loop, run the
NEGATIVE control first — prove the harness reports failure when the defect is
present. If the unflagged/broken case does not fail, nothing after it means
anything. Assert the fixture is in the state the test needs (file exists, is
non-empty, is actually stat-dirty) and fail loudly when it is not. Isolate
trials that mutate shared state. See [[mutation-didnt-fire-suspect-the-test]]
and [[green-suite-is-not-evidence]] — same family, but those are about guards
not firing; this is about the measuring instrument reading zero because it is
unplugged.

input.content:
---
name: git-no-optional-locks-insufficient
description: --no-optional-locks stops git status taking index.lock but NOT git diff <commit>; only plumbing or GIT_INDEX_FILE does
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Measured on git 2.54.0, each trial from an identical stat-dirty index with the
index restored between trials:

    git diff --name-status -M -C HEAD                      REWRITES .git/index
    git --no-optional-locks diff --name-status -M -C HEAD   REWRITES .git/index
    git --no-optional-locks diff-index --name-status …      leaves it alone

A porcelain `git diff <commit>` performs its own index refresh that the
optional-lock setting does not gate. So `--no-optional-locks` closes
`git status` and leaves every worktree-vs-HEAD diff taking the lock.

**Switching to plumbing changes the answer**, so it is not a free swap:
`diff-index` against an unrefreshed index reports a stat-dirty file (mtime
touched, content identical) as modified.

**The fix that keeps both:** point `GIT_INDEX_FILE` at a COPY of the index.
git refreshes the copy, the real index is never opened for write, and the
output is byte-identical to porcelain because it IS porcelain. Verified: copy
output matched real exactly where plumbing differed by one line.

In entire-brain this is `runGitWithScratchIndex` (git_harden.go); it mattered
because `changedSemanticFiles` runs inside `brain brief`, which is what
issue #326 reports colliding with a concurrent git.

Caveat found by CI, not locally: path handling around this must not assume
Unix. `strings.HasPrefix(path, "/")` is true for every absolute path a
macOS/Linux test can build and false for every absolute path on Windows —
see [[verification-harness-false-pass]].

The CI poller is running in the background. Here's the complete picture while it finishes.

## The plan is done

All three PRs are open, stacked, with the Windows fix pushed. **Nothing merged.**

| PR | Scope |
|---|---|
| [#329](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/329) | MCP budget, #325 latency, four silent-failure sites, truncated messages |
| [#330](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/330) | #326, #327, #328, #322, #324 |
| [#331](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/331) | Guide directive, #323, hook wiring, 23 tool descriptions, README |

Plus the **[docs artifact](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/6124d687-c2e5-4fdb-b2ee-4c125cbe8a6d)**.

## CI found a real bug my local suite could not

Three of my new tests failed on `windows-latest` while everything passed locally. Not a test-environment quirk — `relativiseToRepo` checked `strings.HasPrefix(path, "/")`, which is true for every absolute path a macOS or Linux test can construct and **false for every absolute path on Windows**. Ignore matching was silently disabled there, which is the over-reporting mirror of the bug the PR exists to fix. Now handles drive letters and UNC, folds case where the filesystem does, and the guard is a table that runs the Windows forms on every platform.

## The usage experiment — and its limitation

Objective log from a PATH shim, four agents, identical task:

| arm | first tool call |
|---|---|
| new-1 | `graph search` |
| new-2 | `graph search` |
| old-1 | `brain brief` → then `graph query` |
| old-2 | `brain brief` |

**The design doesn't test what the plan asked.** I put the guide text in each agent's prompt, so I measured "does this wording work when forced into context" — not "does the guide file get read and followed". Both arms used the tools, so this cannot reproduce the 0.34% baseline. I can't fix that with subagents, because their project context comes from *my* launch directory, not the worktree they're pointed at.

What it did show: the new wording moved the first action to `graph search` in both cases, and the old guide's agent ran `entire graph query` — **the command that doesn't exist in released 0.4.0**. Live evidence for #323.

The more useful finding is negative, and it's about quality, not usage. In **three of four** runs the agent used the tool as instructed and it failed to find the answer:

> *"The graph search's top hit was the brief-side check, not the real decider. I found `semanticStaleReport` by grep."*
> *"The graph hit was a decoy, so I went to grep."*
> *"The brief only returned loosely related symbols… so I switched to grep."*

Fixing the guide makes agents reach for the tool. On this task, reaching for it didn't pay — grep did. That's worth knowing before concluding the wording fix is sufficient.

I'll report the final CI result when the poller returns.

CI is re-running in the background. The second CI round found a bug worth reporting on its own.

## CI caught something my local suite structurally could not

The `test-cgo` failure was **not** a flake. `gitDiffBinary` returned empty — my scratch-index fix was silently losing worktree edits.

The cause is subtle: git decides whether a cached stat entry is trustworthy by comparing a file's recorded mtime against **the index file's own mtime**. A file changed in the same moment the index was written is "racily clean", and git re-reads it rather than trusting the cache. My copy had a *fresh* mtime, so every tracked file looked safely older, git trusted the stale cache, and a same-size edit came back as unchanged.

That's worse than the lock contention the change exists to fix. Now the copy carries the original's mtime.

What caught it was a **pre-existing hardening test** whose fixture overwrites a 12-byte file with 12 different bytes immediately after committing — exactly the racy window. My own tests sailed past it.

## I wrote a test that wasn't a guard, and threw it away

My first attempt reproduced the scenario directly. It passed. Then I weakened the fix and **it still passed** — it protected nothing. I tried forcing the race by setting mtimes; still didn't fire, because the stat cache invalidates on any mtime mismatch, and the true racy state needs the file's mtime to equal the one `git add` recorded, which isn't portably forceable.

So I deleted it rather than ship protection that doesn't protect, and replaced it with a guard on the **mechanism** — the copy carries the original's mtime — which does fail when the fix is removed:

Done and verified. All three PRs settled identically: **30 checks passing, zero failures**, with the only red being the gate that's yours to clear.

| PR | Checks | Findings | Up to date | Approvals |

| [#329](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/329) → `main` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ awaiting you |

| [#331](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/331) → #330 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ awaiting you |

Agent review found no blocking issues on any of them. Trails [#242](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-brain/trails/242), [#246](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-brain/trails/246), [#247](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-brain/trails/247). **Nothing merged.**

## What shipped

All 14 filed issues and reported problems are addressed across the stack, every fix with a regression test verified by weakening — the guard patched compile-clean, the test shown red, the assertion recorded. Plus the **[docs artifact](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/6124d687-c2e5-4fdb-b2ee-4c125cbe8a6d)** with both tabs.

Measured, not estimated: `status` **24.19s → 2.42s** on the real 961-fact brain; the MCP budget cut from ~52k to ~13k tokens of JSON against a client that refused at ~25k; `FilterWarnings` was discarding **every** index warning in this repo while reporting a clean index.

## Two things to carry forward

**The plan was wrong in five places, and the measurements were worth more than the plan.** The MCP trimming was never broken — it was sized to the transport frame. `--no-optional-locks` doesn't fix #326. The Ollama rejection was never silent. The guide was pinned in three places, and the guide most users get had no Graph obligation at all.

**CI found two bugs my local suite structurally could not** — a Unix-only path check, and a scratch index that silently dropped worktree edits by breaking git's racily-clean detection. I also wrote a test, proved it didn't fire, and deleted it rather than ship protection that doesn't protect.

## What I'd look at next

The experiment's negative result. The guide fix does move the first action to `graph search` — but in three of four runs the agent complied, got a decoy, and grep found the answer instead. Winning the first call is the easy half. I'd spend the next effort on ranking for intent-phrased queries, not more wording. That's written up in the uncommitted `GRAPH-FEEDBACK.md`, with the experiment's own limitation stated plainly: the guide went into the prompt, not the file, so it can't be quoted against the 0.34% baseline.

content.text:
Measured against `origin/main`'s README (362 lines, 15,730 chars). The README shows **34 command forms**; the binary exposes **126**.

## Coverage

| | total | in README | missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top-level commands | 42 | 27 | **15** |
| Subcommands | 84 | 11 | **73** |
| MCP tools (`brain_*`) | 37 | 0 named | **37** |

## Top-level commands with zero mentions

`distill` · `doctor` · `watch` · `stats` · `bundle` · `config` · `gc` · `reset` · `repair` · `patterns` · `entities` · `show` · `multi-get` · `bench` · `version`

Four of those matter more than the rest:

- **`distill`** — the command that extracts durable facts from sessions. It needs an agent, sends transcripts to a model provider, costs money, and can run for hours. It is the mechanism behind "durable facts" and appears nowhere.
- **`doctor`** — the diagnostic you'd want when any of this misbehaves.
- **`watch`** — the README describes "a watcher" five times as a thing setup installs, but never shows the command, so you can't run, inspect, or tune it.
- **`reset` / `gc`** — the only ways to undo or prune. A user whose brain goes wrong has no documented recovery.

## Subcommand families, entirely undocumented

| parent | missing | notable |
|---|---|---|
| `facts` | 14 of 16 | `sync`, `promote`, `review`, `proposals`, `tree`, `map`, `outline`, `files`, `eval*` |
| `inspect` | 11 | `blame`, `regressions`, `boundaries`, `tests`, `trace-path`, `search-graph`, `snippet` |
| `memory` | 11 | `configure`, `jobs`, `rebuild`, `reconcile`, `abstract`, `retry` |
| `workspace` | 10 of 11 | `create`, `add`, `review`, `patterns`, `watch` |
| `privacy` | 6 | `exclude`, `include`, `retention`, `purge`, `verify` — the whole retention-control surface |
| `refresh` | 5 | `index`, `seed`, `sessions`, `history`, `delta` |
| `patterns` | 4 | `refresh`, `skills`, `verify`, `status` |
| `entities` | 4 | `history`, `show`, `backfill`, `migrate` |
| `config` | 3 | `init`, `show`, `path` |
| `bundle` | 2 | `import`, `export` |

`privacy` is the one I'd raise first on principle: six subcommands governing what the brain retains from your sessions, none documented.

## Non-command surface also absent

content.text:
Here's the full accounting. Two of the seven filed issues are **partial**, and their titles ask for more than I delivered — that's the most important thing to know before you review.

## The seven filed issues

| # | Reporter | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 325 | leine4550 | ✅ fixed, measured |
| 326 | peyton-alt | ✅ fixed |
| 323 | leine4550 | ✅ fixed |
| 324 | leine4550 | ✅ fixed |
| 322 | leine4550 | ✅ fixed — **not run on Windows** |
| 327 | peyton-alt | ⚠️ **partial** |
| 328 | peyton-alt | ⚠️ **partial** |

### ⚠️ #327 — "keeps indexing new commits while the worktree has uncommitted changes"

**What I fixed:** a self-inflicted stall. A dirty tree forced a rebuild, the indexer *refused* that rebuild, and a failed refresh aborted the whole watch tick so the cursor never advanced. Nothing progressed at all while the tree stayed dirty. Dirtiness now doesn't force a rebuild it can't perform, and the refusal no longer aborts the tick.

**What I did not fix:** `semantic.go:575` still reads

```go
if dirty && !indexOpts.worktree {
    return errors.New(dirtyWorktreeErrorCode + ": refusing to index uncommitted content without --worktree")
}
```

So when you make a **new commit** with a dirty worktree, the semantic index still refuses to advance to it. The title's literal ask — keep indexing new commits while uncommitted changes exist — needs indexing HEAD via a temp tree, which I didn't build. The watcher no longer wedges, but the index stays behind.

### ⚠️ #328 — "can use Ollama on another machine **and** picks Ollama automatically"

Two asks. I did the second, not the first.

**Fixed:** `defaultRefreshAgent` tried codex → claude → none, with ollama absent entirely. Someone who installed a local model to keep transcripts off a third party got no distillation, or — if a cloud CLI happened to be present — their sessions sent to that provider. ollama is now tried first. `watch` hardcoded `codex`, worse because it runs unattended; now auto-detects.

**Not done:** a non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL` is still rejected. The loopback restriction is a deliberate privacy boundary with a redirect guard behind it, so opening it is a product decision rather than a bug fix. Say the word and I'll add an opt-in flag.

Also worth flagging: the issue says the rejection is *silent*. It isn't — it's a hard error naming the URL. That premise was wrong.

### The four clean ones

**#325** — `status --json` ran `git for-each-ref --contains` per anchor commit, a full history walk, on every call once facts existed. Gated behind the existing `--details`. **24.19s → 2.42s** on the real 961-fact brain.

**#326** — `brain brief` took `.git/index.lock`. `--no-optional-locks` turned out *not* to be enough: a porcelain `git diff <commit>` does its own index refresh the flag doesn't gate. The fix points `GIT_INDEX_FILE` at a copy — lock-free and byte-identical to porcelain, where switching to plumbing would have changed the answer.

**#323** — the generated guide recommended `entire graph query`, absent from released v0.4.0. It worked here only because the installed binary is a symlink to a dev checkout. Now emits `search`, correct on both.

**#324** — `facts promote --keep-both` emitted `Confidence: 0` as a literal with no similarity ever computed, one proposal per *pair*. Now computed, with a spanning set (n−1 edges, not n(n−1)/2), capped relative to the auto-apply threshold so it can never become auto-applyable.

**#322** — a 7,516-byte system prompt on argv against cmd.exe's 8,191 limit. Moved off argv at the shared builder. Tests are platform-independent, but **a real Windows run is still needed** to close it.

## Problems fixed that nobody filed

These came from the transcripts and a sweep, not the issue tracker:

| Problem | Why it mattered |
|---|---|
| **MCP tools returned results no client accepts** | `brain_status`, `brain_brief`, `brain_impact` all errored. The budget was sized to the 4 MiB transport frame, not the context window — 128 KiB of this JSON is ~52k tokens, double a client's ceiling. A context-saving tool that overflows context is worse than no tool. |
| **`FilterWarnings` discarded every index warning** | It matched `.brainignore` patterns against free prose by substring. This repo's line 1 is `entire-brain`, a substring of every absolute path under it — so status reported a clean index that had silently missed files. |
| **Guide told agents not to use the tools** | And CI enforced it: the test *banned* `"FIRST action"`/`"SEARCH FIRST"` and *required* `"sufficient locations"`. Measured cost: 332 graph calls against 96,987 exploration calls. |
| **`hook pre-edit` shipped and was never called** | Since PR #24. The only push path in an otherwise pull-only product. |
| **37 MCP tools, none saying when to use them instead of grep** | The description is what an agent reads when choosing. |
| **regression / export / distill dropped work silently** | A capped scan printed "No suspected regressions"; export counted the *filtered* warning set; distill's 50-entry cap ran *before* persisting, so warning 51 existed nowhere. |
| **Three status messages cut mid-word** | A 140-**byte** width on a rune string. One was reported as a typo. |

## Two bugs I introduced, and CI caught

Worth knowing because they say something about the test suite:

- **Unix-only path check** — `HasPrefix(path, "/")` is true for every absolute path a macOS or Linux test can build and false for every absolute path on Windows. Ignore matching was silently off there.
- **Scratch index lost worktree edits** — copying the index gave it a fresh mtime, which breaks git's racily-clean detection, so a same-size edit read as unchanged. Worse than the lock problem it fixed. Caught by a *pre-existing* hardening test; all of mine sailed past.

## Which PR holds what

- **[#329](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/329)** — MCP budget, #325, the four silent-failure sites, truncated messages, Windows path fix
- **[#330](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/330)** — #326, #327 (partial), #328 (partial), #322, #324, scratch-index mtime fix
- **[#331](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/331)** — guide directive, #323, hook wiring, tool descriptions, README

Good — the PR doesn't claim it. Its verification section only claims the guards are weakening-verified, and attributes the 0.34% to graph's own measurement. So nothing durable overclaims. But to your question:

## I did not verify that usage will increase

What I ran was four subagents, two per arm, same task, with tool calls logged objectively by a PATH shim:

| arm | first tool call |
|---|---|
| directive guide ×2 | `entire graph search` |
| permissive guide ×2 | `entire brain brief` |

Four reasons that doesn't support the claim:

**1. The confound that invalidates it.** I put the guide text **into each agent's prompt**, not into `.entire/agent-guide.md`. The real-world failure is that the guide *file* doesn't get read or followed. I tested whether the wording works when it's already in context — which is the one condition that was never in doubt. I couldn't test the file path because a subagent's project context comes from *my* launch directory, not the worktree I point it at.

**2. No headroom.** Both arms used the tools 100% of the time. If the baseline is 0.34%, an experiment where the control arm scores 100% isn't measuring the same thing. What differed was *which* tool went first, not *whether* one was used.

**3. n=2 per arm.** By my own benchmark notes the minimum detectable effect is ~25 points at n=30. At n=2 there is no inference to make. One task, one repo, one model.

**4. Favourable task selection.** I gave them a pure locate-and-explain task — the case the tool is designed for. That's the most generous possible setting.

## What the causal evidence actually is

Two things, neither controlled:

- **An association.** 332 graph calls against 96,987 exploration calls, graph-first rate 0, measured *after* the permissive wording shipped. Nobody measured before. I phrased it as "measured afterwards" in the PR, which is accurate, but it is not a before/after.
- **A self-report.** A Claude session in the transcript said: *"The agent guide says to start substantive tasks with `entire brain brief` and use Graph for code discovery. I skipped that."* Strong as a mechanism hint, worthless as a rate.

What I *can* claim with confidence is narrower and all structural: the guide said the opposite of what was intended, CI enforced that in both directions, `combinedWorkflow` carried no Graph obligation at all, and the command it named doesn't exist in the released version. Those are facts about the text, verified by weakening. Whether fixing them moves behaviour is a separate question I didn't answer.

## And I found counter-evidence

This is the part I'd weight most heavily. In **three of four** runs the agent used the tool as instructed and it failed:

> *"The graph search's top hit was the brief-side check, not the real decider. I found `semanticStaleReport` by grep."*
> *"The graph hit was a decoy, so I went to grep."*
> *"The brief only returned loosely related symbols… so I switched to grep."*

Same decoy twice — `brainBriefSemanticNeedsCurrentBoundary` ranks first for "decide whether the semantic index needs rebuilding" and is not that decision. Grep found the real answer every time.

So even granting that the directive wins the first call, an agent that complies, gets a decoy, and succeeds with grep has learned the tool doesn't pay. I'd expect compliance to decay. **Fixing the wording may raise first-call rate while leaving sustained usage flat** — and nothing I ran can distinguish those.

## What would actually verify it

1. Install the guide as a **file** via `init-agents` in a real repo — the condition that's actually broken.
