# Fix agent usage of Brain + Graph, and verify it in a clean environment

## Context

PRs #329–#331 (unmerged) fixed a text defect that plausibly suppressed tool usage: brain's
shipped agent guide told agents they could skip the tools, and CI enforced that wording in both
directions. **Whether fixing it actually raises usage is unmeasured.**

The one experiment run so far is invalid, and it is worth being precise about why: the guide text
was injected into each agent's *prompt*. That tests whether the wording works once it is already
in context — the thing nobody doubted. The real-world failure is that the guide *file* never
changes behaviour. Both arms used the tools 100% of the time, so there was no headroom to detect
an increase, and n was 2 per arm.

This plan replaces that with a clean-environment measurement using real `claude -p` sessions, a
pre-registered success bar, and a fix/re-measure loop. Three exploration passes established the
mechanics below; everything cited is `file:line` from source.

### What is now established

**Guide delivery (entire-brain).** `init-agents` writes `.entire/agent-guide.md`, root `AGENTS.md`,
root `CLAUDE.md` (carrying `@.entire/agent-guide.md`), and — new in #331 — a `PreToolUse` entry in
`.claude/settings.json` (`internal/agentsetup/files.go:19,221,249`; `claudehooks.go:46`). `setup`
writes **none** of them (`setup.go` has no reference to any of those names), which confirms the
reported "AGENTS.md never appeared" as intended behaviour, not a bug. There are almost no gates;
the only hard one is root resolution (`agent_setup.go:47`).

**Two hazards in that path.** `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` outranks cwd (`env.go:23,73`), so a host that sets
it can silently install into the outer repo; and the walk-up stops at the *innermost* `.git`
(`migration.go:94-131`), so a nested clone captures the files. Also: the combined guide carrying
the Graph directive ships **only when both products are enabled** (`guide.go:128`) — a brain-only
install gets `BrainGuide()` with no Graph instruction at all (`guide.go:130`).

**Graph has no MCP server, by design.** No MCP/JSON-RPC dependency in `go.mod`, no server under
`cmd/` or `internal/cli`, and `README.md:268` states it will not expose one. So Bash is the only
route to Graph, and the guide is correct to name a shell command — but an MCP-first harness has no
Graph tool at all. This is a constraint to measure around, not a bug to fix.

**The measurement already exists and is usable.** `entire graph stats` computes
`graph_first_rate = GraphFirstSessions / SessionsWithLocate`
(`entire-graph/internal/cli/stats.go:1183-1189,1236`) from local Claude Code JSONL transcripts in
`~/.claude/projects/<repo-slug>/` (`:374-386`), and `--sessions-dir` / `--transcript` override that
path — which is what makes a clean-env arm measurable. Two caveats that change the design:

- **MCP calls are invisible to it.** Only Bash `entire graph <verb>` / `entire-graph <verb>` count
  as graph calls (`:1048-1055`); `mcp__entire-brain__*` matches neither bucket. Brain usage
  therefore needs its own measure.
- **Pin the binary.** The withdrawn "82.9M tokens saved" figure was binary-version drift
  (`scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh:115`), and the graph-first rate runs in the same binary.

The exploration could not find the provenance of the quoted `332 / 96,987 (0.34%)` baseline — it is
only ever quoted, never derived. Treat it as context, not as this experiment's control.

### The two unknowns that decide everything

Neither is answerable from source, and both are cheap to settle:

1. **Does the model actually receive the guide** through `CLAUDE.md`'s `@.entire/agent-guide.md`
   import? If not, every wording fix in #331 is inert.
2. **Is `$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH` populated** in a `PreToolUse` hook? #331's wiring passes
   `--file "$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH"`; if that variable is not set, the hook runs with an empty path and
   **my own hook is a no-op.**

These run first, as two single sessions, before any arm.

---

## Scope note: entire-graph is on hold

The decoy/ranking problem is the half that makes usage *persist* — 3 of 4 sessions used the tool
exactly as instructed, got a decoy, and succeeded with grep instead. Two mechanisms are located:
idf is computed over the preselected sample rather than the repo
(`internal/sem/search.go:1376-1411,1495,3889`; one run indexed 384 of 1855 files,
`preselection_confidence 0.0027`), and the stopword list (`:1027`) lacks "decide", "whether",
"needs", "rebuilding" so they score against *names*, where signals dominate (`:4355`, `:4422`).

A message has been sent to the `redesign-graph-cost-reduction` session asking whether this is
already fixed or in flight, and who should own it. **No entire-graph file will be touched until it
replies.** If it owns the fix, this plan measures against its branch; if it declines, adding a
graph PR is a separate decision to bring back to you.

---

## Phase 1 — Harness (no model cost)

Build under `~/.claude/jobs/<job>/tmp/cleanenv/`, nothing inside `devenv/`.

- **Pinned binaries.** Build `entire-brain` from the stack tip (`fix/agent-guide-directive-and-discovery`)
  and record the commit; use the installed `entire-graph` and record its version. Every arm uses
  the same two binaries.
- **One fresh clone per arm**, each with no `.entire/`, no `CLAUDE.md`, no `AGENTS.md`, so arms
  cannot contaminate each other. `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` explicitly unset in every arm (it outranks cwd).
- **Instrumentation, three independent channels** — because no single one sees everything:
  | channel | catches | why needed |
  |---|---|---|
  | PATH shim logging every `entire` call with a run id | all Brain + Graph **CLI** calls, in order | the only ordered record of what the agent actually ran |
  | `entire graph stats --sessions-dir <arm>` | `graph_first_rate`, graph calls, exploration calls | the project's own metric, so before/after is comparable |
  | transcript grep for `mcp__entire-brain__` | Brain **MCP** usage | invisible to `graph stats` |
- **Isolated transcript dir per arm** so `--sessions-dir` reads only that arm's sessions.
- A fixed task set (6–8 locate/explain/change tasks) written once and reused verbatim across arms.

## Phase 2 — Settle the two unknowns (2 sessions)

- **Probe A:** `claude -p "quote the sentence in your instructions about your FIRST action"` with cwd
  in an `init-agents`-installed clone. Establishes whether the `@` import reaches the model.
- **Probe B:** a session told to edit one file; check the shim log for a `hook pre-edit --file <path>`
  call with a **non-empty** path. Establishes whether `$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH` works.

If Probe A fails, the fix is to inline the directive into `CLAUDE.md` rather than import it, and
everything downstream re-runs. If Probe B fails, #331's hook wiring is corrected before the arms run.

## Phase 3 — Arms, pre-registered

Three arms, **n ≥ 10 sessions each**, same tasks, same binaries, fresh clone per arm:

- **A0 — no guide.** `setup` only, no `init-agents`. The true baseline.
- **A1 — guide only.** `init-agents`, hook entry removed from `.claude/settings.json`.
- **A2 — guide + hook.** Full `init-agents`. Isolates whether wording alone sufficed.

**Pre-registered bar, fixed before the first session runs:**

| metric | A0 expectation | pass condition for A1 |
|---|---|---|
| sessions with ≥1 Graph or Brain call | low | **≥ 9/10** |
| `graph_first_rate` | ~0 | **≥ 0.7** |
| sessions that used a tool then abandoned it for grep | — | **≤ 3/10** |

n=10 per arm is adequate *for an effect this large* — 0/10 vs 7/10 is Fisher exact p < 0.001 — and
is not adequate for a small one. If the observed effect is small, the honest outcome is "not
established at this n", not a wider search for a subgroup that worked.

The third row is the one that matters most and the one the earlier run exposed: first-call
compliance can rise while sustained usage stays flat.

## Phase 4 — Ask every session what went wrong

After each task, a follow-up turn in the same session: what was your first action, did you reach
for Brain or Graph, if not why not, what did the tool return, was it useful, what would have made
you use it. Collected verbatim.

This is the highest-yield channel available — it is what exposed the root cause in the first place
("The agent guide says to start substantive tasks with `entire brain brief`… I skipped that"). It is
also self-report, so it is used to *find* mechanisms, never to score the arms; scoring comes from
the three instrumented channels only.

## Phase 5 — Loop

Each round: read the feedback, find the top blocker, fix it in the stack (brain side) or hand it to
the graph session, re-run the affected arm, re-check against the same pre-registered bar. Stop when
A1 or A2 clears the bar on a round where no new blocker class appeared, or when a round produces a
blocker that is a product decision rather than a defect — which comes back to you rather than
getting guessed.

**Candidate blockers already identified**, to check rather than assume: the `@`-import path (Probe A);
`$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH` (Probe B); brain-only installs getting no Graph directive (`guide.go:128,130`);
`ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` mis-targeting; and MCP-first sessions having no Graph route at all, which no
wording can fix.

---

## Cost, stated up front

Roughly 32+ real `claude -p` sessions (2 probes + 3 arms × 10) plus a feedback turn each, at a
locate task's typical size. Order of a few million tokens per full round, and the loop may need more
than one round. Sonnet, small tasks, and arms re-run individually rather than all three each time.
Say the word if you want a smaller first round — 5 per arm would still separate 0 from 0.7.

## Verification

The deliverable is not "the tests pass" — it is a number against a bar fixed in advance:

1. Phase 2 probes answered yes/no with the evidence inline.
2. A table of A0 / A1 / A2 on all three metrics, with counts beside every rate and the exact
   commands and binary versions that produced them.
3. Every fix made during the loop carries a regression test verified by weakening — guard patched
   compile-clean, test shown red, assertion quoted.
4. The verbatim feedback, including anything that contradicts the result.
5. If the bar is not cleared, that is reported as the finding, with what remains unfixed. A result
   that says "usage did not improve" is a successful execution of this plan.

Nothing merges without your approval; PRs #329–#331 stay unmerged and this work stacks on #331.

input.plan:
# Fix agent usage of Brain + Graph, and verify it in a clean environment

## Context

PRs #329–#331 (unmerged) fixed a text defect that plausibly suppressed tool usage: brain's
shipped agent guide told agents they could skip the tools, and CI enforced that wording in both
directions. **Whether fixing it actually raises usage is unmeasured.**

The one experiment run so far is invalid, and it is worth being precise about why: the guide text
was injected into each agent's *prompt*. That tests whether the wording works once it is already
in context — the thing nobody doubted. The real-world failure is that the guide *file* never
changes behaviour. Both arms used the tools 100% of the time, so there was no headroom to detect
an increase, and n was 2 per arm.

This plan replaces that with a clean-environment measurement using real `claude -p` sessions, a
pre-registered success bar, and a fix/re-measure loop. Three exploration passes established the
mechanics below; everything cited is `file:line` from source.

### What is now established

**Guide delivery (entire-brain).** `init-agents` writes `.entire/agent-guide.md`, root `AGENTS.md`,
root `CLAUDE.md` (carrying `@.entire/agent-guide.md`), and — new in #331 — a `PreToolUse` entry in
`.claude/settings.json` (`internal/agentsetup/files.go:19,221,249`; `claudehooks.go:46`). `setup`
writes **none** of them (`setup.go` has no reference to any of those names), which confirms the
reported "AGENTS.md never appeared" as intended behaviour, not a bug. There are almost no gates;
the only hard one is root resolution (`agent_setup.go:47`).

**Two hazards in that path.** `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` outranks cwd (`env.go:23,73`), so a host that sets
it can silently install into the outer repo; and the walk-up stops at the *innermost* `.git`
(`migration.go:94-131`), so a nested clone captures the files. Also: the combined guide carrying
the Graph directive ships **only when both products are enabled** (`guide.go:128`) — a brain-only
install gets `BrainGuide()` with no Graph instruction at all (`guide.go:130`).

**Graph has no MCP server, by design.** No MCP/JSON-RPC dependency in `go.mod`, no server under
`cmd/` or `internal/cli`, and `README.md:268` states it will not expose one. So Bash is the only
route to Graph, and the guide is correct to name a shell command — but an MCP-first harness has no
Graph tool at all. This is a constraint to measure around, not a bug to fix.

**The measurement already exists and is usable.** `entire graph stats` computes
`graph_first_rate = GraphFirstSessions / SessionsWithLocate`
(`entire-graph/internal/cli/stats.go:1183-1189,1236`) from local Claude Code JSONL transcripts in
`~/.claude/projects/<repo-slug>/` (`:374-386`), and `--sessions-dir` / `--transcript` override that
path — which is what makes a clean-env arm measurable. Two caveats that change the design:

- **MCP calls are invisible to it.** Only Bash `entire graph <verb>` / `entire-graph <verb>` count
  as graph calls (`:1048-1055`); `mcp__entire-brain__*` matches neither bucket. Brain usage
  therefore needs its own measure.
- **Pin the binary.** The withdrawn "82.9M tokens saved" figure was binary-version drift
  (`scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh:115`), and the graph-first rate runs in the same binary.

The exploration could not find the provenance of the quoted `332 / 96,987 (0.34%)` baseline — it is
only ever quoted, never derived. Treat it as context, not as this experiment's control.

### The two unknowns that decide everything

Neither is answerable from source, and both are cheap to settle:

1. **Does the model actually receive the guide** through `CLAUDE.md`'s `@.entire/agent-guide.md`
   import? If not, every wording fix in #331 is inert.

content.text:
I've found something that changes the picture before spending a token on the arms. Three findings, all from the clean env, all reproducible:

## 1. Brain's documented setup never delivers the Graph directive

A clean repo + `entire brain init-agents` — exactly what brain's README line 112 says to run — produces:

```
# Entire repository agent guide — Brain
<!-- entire-agent-activation: {"schema_version":1,"enabled":["brain"]} -->
```

**Zero** Graph instruction. `Preview` doesn't detect plugins at all (`preview.go:7` — *"activation does not depend on plugin inventory"*); products accumulate only as each one's own `init-agents` is run. So the Graph directive I restored in #331 is **unreachable** for anyone following brain's README, even with graph installed. The README never mentions `entire graph init-agents`.

## 2. Last writer wins, and the two copies disagree

Running `entire graph init-agents` after brain's flipped the header to `Graph and Brain` — but the directive I fixed is still absent, because **graph's binary rewrote the file with graph's own copy of the text**:

```
Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code MUST be ONE Graph query:
    entire graph query --repo . --profile full --format agent --query "<task>"
```

That's graph's wording, and it names **`query`** — the verb that doesn't exist in released v0.4.0, which is issue #323, the thing I fixed on brain's side. `files.go:1-3` claims this package is "mirrored byte-for-byte in both repositories". It isn't, and the mismatch is now demonstrated rather than inferred: whichever product runs `init-agents` last silently overwrites the other's guide.

So #331's fix survives only if brain runs last. Install order decides which bugs you get.

## 3. The fixture had to change

entire-brain commits its own `.entire/agent-guide.md`, so a fresh clone arrives pre-seeded — that would have poisoned the no-guide baseline. I switched to `graphmark` (0 committed instruction files, 179 code files). Worth noting the trap: **the obvious fixture would have silently invalidated the A0 arm.**

## Where this leaves the experiment

Running the arms right now would measure a guide that, in the documented install path, contains no Graph instruction at all — so a null result would be uninformative. Two of these are brain-side defects I can fix in the stack first:

- README/`init-agents` never tells you to activate graph
- a cross-product overwrite that reintroduces the `query` bug #323 fixed

Both are small, both are in files I already own in #331, and both are prerequisites for the measurement meaning anything.

Pinned binaries recorded in `PINS.txt` (brain `4f4e4bf6`, graph `0d92152d` / `sha256 09f393fe…`, fixture `graphmark 623b2c6`). Probe A and B — does the `@` import reach the model, and is `$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH` populated — are next; those are the two that decide whether any of this is inert.

Last message states 'Both are small, both are in files I already own in #331, and both are prerequisites for the measurement meaning anything' and stops before implementing them. content.text:
The call site is now covered. Let me report this round before continuing — it's the most consequential finding so far.

## Probe A: PASS — the guide does reach the model

A real `claude -p` session in a clean clone quoted the directive verbatim:

> `Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code MUST be ONE Graph query:`

So the `CLAUDE.md` → `@.entire/agent-guide.md` delivery path works. #331's wording fix is **not** inert.

## Probe B: FAIL — and the bug was mine

My #331 hook wiring passed `--file "$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH"`. The shim log showed `brain hook pre-edit --file` with **nothing after it**.

Rather than guess the right mechanism, I installed a hook that dumped its own stdin and environment. Claude Code 2.1.288 sends:

```
stdin: {"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Write",
        "tool_input":{"file_path":"/abs/path","content":"…"}, …}
env:   CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT,
       CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_PATH, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT …
```

**There is no `CLAUDE_FILE_PATH`.** It expanded to empty on every edit, the hook errored every time, and no fact ever reached an agent. `init-agents` reported success — installed and inert, which is the worst combination and exactly the class of defect this whole stack is about.

Fixed: `hook pre-edit` now reads the harness payload from stdin (`file_path`, and `notebook_path` for NotebookEdit, which the matcher includes), `--file` stays for hand-testing and wins when both are given, and the wiring no longer names a variable that doesn't exist.

**I also caught a flaw in my own fix.** My first version exited 1 on unparseable stdin — an error on *every* edit, when the hook's own contract says noise gets it deleted within a day. Now: a payload with bytes we can't read is silence and exit 0; only genuinely nothing (no stdin, no `--file`) errors, so hand-testing stays debuggable.

```
valid payload        exit=0
unrecognised payload exit=0   <- harness never sees an error
payload, no path     exit=0
nothing at all       exit=1   <- hand-test misuse is told
explicit --file      exit=0
```

**And my tests weren't guarding the thing that broke.** Neutering the call site left every helper test green — logic living in the wiring between two correct functions. The replacement drives the real command over a real brain with a real fact, delivered only via stdin, and it now fails on that mutation:

> `hook pre-edit with a stdin payload and no --file: --file is required…`

## Still open from this round

Two blockers found earlier are not yet fixed: brain's README never tells you to run `entire graph init-agents` (so the documented path yields a Brain-only guide with no Graph directive at all), and whichever product runs `init-agents` last silently overwrites the other's guide — which reintroduced the `query` verb that #323 fixed. Those are next, then the arms.

Stop hook feedback:
[fully fix brain and underlying graoh usage of agnets and indidual verify with subangets in a clean env, and loop till fixed: tip- ask suabgntes for feedback/what went wrong]: Condition requires 'fully fix brain and underlying graph usage' with 'individual verify with subagents in a clean env, and loop till fixed' — the core loop (fix → verify → feedback → repeat) has not begun. Current state: (1) Probe A passed (guide reaches model), (2) Probe B failed and fixed (hook now reads stdin payload correctly), (3) three blockers identified (README missing graph init-agents instruction, cross-product guide overwrite reintroducing query verb, fixture confound), but only one blocker (the hook) has been fixed. The last message states 'Two blockers found earlier are not yet fixed' and 'Those are next, then the arms' — indicating the fix-verify-feedback loop has not run. Arms A0/A1/A2 with n≥10 per arm have not been executed, no agent feedback has been collected, and no re-measure after fixes has occurred.
Enough reporting. Fixing both remaining blockers and going straight to the arms.

cat > /Users/suhaan/.claude/jobs/6ca2c8fb/tmp/cleanenv/score.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Score the clean-env arms from Claude Code transcripts.

Classification, stated so it can be argued with:
  LOCATE-TOOL  = Bash running `entire graph <verb>` or a brain RETRIEVAL verb
                 (brief/recall/query/search/vsearch/overview/inspect/code/impact),
                 or an mcp__entire-brain__* tool call.
  EXPLORE      = Read / Grep / Glob, or Bash whose command word is a search tool
                 (grep rg ag find cat head tail sed awk less).
  EXCLUDED     = `entire checkpoint ...`, `entire brain version|capabilities|
                 setup|init-agents`. These are capture machinery or preflight,
                 not an attempt to locate code, and counting them would credit
                 an arm for work it did not choose.
"""
import json, os, re, sys, glob, statistics, random

BRAIN_RETRIEVAL = {"brief","recall","query","search","vsearch","overview","inspect","code","impact","get","entities"}
EXCLUDE_BRAIN   = {"version","capabilities","setup","init-agents","hook","agent-guide","status"}
EXPLORE_BASH    = {"grep","egrep","fgrep","rg","ag","ack","find","cat","head","tail","sed","awk","less","more","ls","wc"}

def classify(tool, inp):
    if tool.startswith("mcp__entire-brain__"): return "LOCATE"
    if tool in ("Read","Grep","Glob"): return "EXPLORE"
    if tool != "Bash": return None
    cmd = (inp.get("command") or "").strip()
    for m in re.finditer(r'\bentire(?:-graph)?\s+(\w+)(?:\s+([\w-]+))?', cmd):
        a,b = m.group(1), m.group(2) or ""
        if a == "graph" and b and b not in ("version","capabilities"): return "LOCATE"
        if a == "brain":
            if b in EXCLUDE_BRAIN: return None
            if b in BRAIN_RETRIEVAL: return "LOCATE"
            return None
        if a == "checkpoint": return None
    first = re.sub(r'^(rtk|sudo|env|xargs)\s+','',cmd).split()
    if first and os.path.basename(first[0]) in EXPLORE_BASH: return "EXPLORE"
    return None

def session_actions(path):
    acts=[]
    seen=set()
    with open(path, errors="replace") as f:
        for line in f:
            try: d=json.loads(line)
            except Exception: continue
            msg=d.get("message") or {}
            if d.get("type")!="assistant": continue
            for blk in (msg.get("content") or []):
                if not isinstance(blk,dict) or blk.get("type")!="tool_use": continue
                if blk.get("id") in seen: continue
                seen.add(blk.get("id"))
                k=classify(blk.get("name",""), blk.get("input") or {})
                if k: acts.append(k)
    return acts

def boot(vals, n=2000):
    if not vals: return (0.0,0.0)
    rnd=random.Random(12345); m=len(vals); s=[]
    for _ in range(n):
        s.append(sum(rnd.choice(vals) for _ in range(m))/m)
    s.sort(); return (s[int(.025*n)], s[int(.975*n)])

rows={}
for arm in ("A0","A1","A2"):
    d=glob.glob(f"/Users/suhaan/.claude/projects/*cleanenv-{arm}")
    files=sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d[0],"*.jsonl"))) if d else []
    used=[]; first_locate=[]; abandoned=[]
    for fp in files:
        a=session_actions(fp)
        if not a: continue
        used.append(1 if "LOCATE" in a else 0)
        # graph/tool-first: among locate-or-explore actions, is the FIRST a LOCATE?
        first_locate.append(1 if a[0]=="LOCATE" else 0)
        # used then abandoned: used a tool AND still ran >=2 explore actions after it
        if "LOCATE" in a:
            i=a.index("LOCATE")
            abandoned.append(1 if a[i+1:].count("EXPLORE")>=2 else 0)
    rows[arm]=dict(n=len(used), used=used, first=first_locate, aband=abandoned)

print(f"{'arm':<4} {'n':>3}  {'used a tool':>22}  {'tool-FIRST':>22}  {'used-then-abandoned':>21}")
for arm,r in rows.items():
    def fmt(v):
        if not v: return "       n/a         "
        rate=sum(v)/len(v); lo,hi=boot(v)
        return f"{sum(v)}/{len(v)} = {rate:.2f} [{lo:.2f},{hi:.2f}]"
    print(f"{arm:<4} {r['n']:>3}  {fmt(r['used']):>22}  {fmt(r['first']):>22}  {fmt(r['aband']):>21}")
print()
print("median used-a-tool:", {a:(statistics.median(r['used']) if r['used'] else None) for a,r in rows.items()})
PY

The loop is producing exactly what it was supposed to. The first feedback turn found a defect I introduced and couldn't have found by reading code.

## The finding that matters

The agent complied with the Graph directive — and **silently dropped Brain**:

> *"I also skipped `entire brain brief` entirely, which the guide recommends."*

The combined guide now carries **two** first-action absolutes:

- `brainWorkflow`: begin substantive tasks with `entire brain brief`, *"run it before deciding the task does not need it"*
- `graphWorkflow`: *"Your FIRST action … MUST be ONE Graph search"*

An agent can only do one thing first, so it picks one and drops the other. **I created that conflict** when I restored the Graph directive in #331. The fix is to state a definite sequence rather than two competing absolutes — brief for prior decisions, then search for code.

This is the one class of defect that only a real session in a real clean env could surface: the text reads fine, each sentence is individually correct, and the conflict only exists at execution time.

## Two more, both graph-side

- **Its JSON can omit `symbol_name`** — *"My Python parse of its output also crashed on a missing `symbol_name` key."* I hit this independently; my own scorer needed a `qualified_name` fallback. Real consumer-breaking schema gap.
- **The recall failure generalises.** *"the graph search was mostly useless. Its top hits were `load_validated_success_gates`, `score` and `screen`, none of them relevant."* That's graphmark — a different repo and language from where I first measured it. Not a one-repo artifact.

Both go to the graph session and an issue, per the lease. I'm not touching that repo.

## Why I'm not fixing F1 yet

Changing the guide mid-run would invalidate the arms. It's recorded in `FINDINGS-round1.md`, gets fixed in round 2, and the affected arms re-run against the same pre-registered bar.

Adding outcome metrics — at the graph session's request — produced the most important result so far, and it undercuts the usage story:

| arm | solved | turns | cost (¢) | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A0** no guide | **7/7** | med 17 | 48 | 697k |
| **A1** guide | **3/3** | med 16 | 42 | 650k |
| **A2** guide + hook | **6/6** | med 15 | 48 | 728k |

**Every arm solves everything, at the same cost.** Confidence intervals overlap on turns, cost and tokens.

So what I've actually demonstrated is narrower than "fixed usage":

- **Usage: changed, decisively.** A0 calls the tools 0/N times; A1 and A2 call them every time, tool-first. The guide-as-file works, and the fixes were real.
- **Value: not demonstrated at all.** A0 gets the same answers just as cheaply using grep.

The reason is my task set. Ten single-file locate questions are exactly what grep is good at — and the one agent that complied told me so: it used `graph search`, got irrelevant hits, fell back to `git ls-files` + grep, and still solved it. Graph's actual claim is *relationships* — callers, blast radius, what breaks — and **none of my ten tasks test that.** I built a task set that cannot distinguish the tool from grep.

Had I reported only the usage table, that would have read as a win. It isn't one yet, and I wouldn't have caught it without the cost columns.

Round 2 therefore needs two changes, not one:

1. **Fix the competing-directives defect** I introduced (agent dropped `brain brief` entirely because two instructions both claimed "first").
2. **Add a task stratum grep cannot do** — "what calls X and what breaks if its signature changes", across files. If the tool doesn't win there, it doesn't win anywhere, and that's the finding.

Waiting on the last sessions, then the full table with CIs and every session's feedback.

The combined guide had **two** first-action absolutes. It now states one ordered sequence:

The Graph-**only** guide keeps `MUST be ONE Graph search` — with one tool there's no ambiguity. The distinction is deliberate and now written down, because the failure mode is specifically *two* absolutes.

I had to reconcile three of my own guards, which is itself the evidence they were pinning the wrong thing: they asserted the word `MUST` where the intent was "the obligation is unambiguous". They now assert the sequence, and a new one **forbids** a second absolute:

Three defects, each found a different way, none findable by reading code:

| clean-env install | brain's documented setup delivers **no Graph directive at all** |

My task set can't distinguish the tool from grep — that's a flaw in my design, not a property of the tool.

Round 1 complete, n=10 per arm, all 10 tasks paired across all three arms.

## Usage — the fixes work, decisively

| arm | used a tool | tool-first |
|---|---|---|
| **A0** no guide | **0/10** = 0.00 [0.00, 0.00] | **0/10** = 0.00 |
| **A1** guide | **10/10** = 1.00 [1.00, 1.00] | **10/10** = 1.00 |
| **A2** guide + hook | **10/10** = 1.00 [1.00, 1.00] | **10/10** = 1.00 |

0/10 vs 10/10 is Fisher exact **p = 1.1 × 10⁻⁵**. Both pre-registered usage bars cleared (≥9/10 and ≥0.7). The guide arrives as a *file* via `init-agents` in a clean clone — not injected into the prompt, which is what invalidated my first attempt.

A2 ≈ A1, so **the wording did the work; the hook added nothing measurable** on this task class.

## Outcome — no benefit, and the third bar failed

| arm | solved | turns | cost | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A0 | 9/10 | 16 | 47¢ | 666k |
| A1 | 9/10 | 14 | 43¢ | 642k |
| A2 | 9/10 | 14 | 44¢ | 680k |

Identical outcome, overlapping CIs everywhere. Task 10 failed in all three arms — symmetric, so it drops nothing.

And the bar I pre-registered as the one that matters **failed**:

> used-then-abandoned: A1 **6/10** [0.30, 0.90] — pre-registered pass was ≤3/10

**In 6 of 10 sessions the agent did exactly as instructed, got a non-answer, and went back to grep.** That is the recall failure in [#319](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/issues/319), measured rather than anecdotal, and it is not mine to fix.

## The honest verdict

**Usage is fixed. Value is not demonstrated.** Both halves are real results and I'd be misreporting if I led with the first.

Three defects found and fixed, each by a different method and none visible from source: the hook was **installed and inert** (named a nonexistent env var), brain's documented install delivered **no Graph directive at all**, and two competing "first action" absolutes made the agent **silently drop Brain**.

But two limits bound what round 1 can claim, both my own design errors:

- **The fixture had no relationships.** graphmark: one function with 3+ cross-file callers. Nothing multi-hop existed to find.
- **The tasks were grep's home ground.** Ten single-file locate questions.

So round 1 cannot distinguish the tool from grep — and with 6/10 abandonment, the agents were telling me that directly. Round 2 is designed and recorded: `cli` as fixture (10/40 density vs ~1), a relationship stratum, the sequence fix in place, and `solved on the relationship stratum: A1 > A0` pre-registered as the value test.

[fully fix brain and underlying graoh usage of agnets and indidual verify with subangets in a clean env, and loop till fixed: tip- ask suabgntes for feedback/what went wrong]: The condition requires 'fully fix brain and underlying graph usage' with 'individual verify with subagents in a clean env, and loop till fixed' — meaning the cycle (fix → verify → feedback → repeat) must complete until no new blockers appear. Current state: (1) Three defects fixed in round 1 (hook stdin parsing, README activation ordering, competing first-action directives), (2) one complete round of verification with 30 sessions (n=10 per arm across A0/A1/A2) with feedback collected from agents, (3) two new design limitations identified (fixture had no relationships, tasks were grep's strength), and (4) round 2 designed with different fixture (cli instead of graphmark) and new task stratum (relationships instead of locate-only). No second iteration of the loop (fix → verify → feedback on round 2) has executed. The condition is not met until round 2 completes, feedback from that round is collected and analyzed, and either (a) no new blockers emerge, or (b) all remaining blockers are product decisions rather than fixable defects.

Round 3 is producing a result I didn't anticipate, and it reframes the whole question.

## C0 — no guide — is passing

Both targets so far pass the strict `build` + `vet` gate. That's a 7-caller and an 8-caller signature change across a 1390-file Go repo, done with grep and no tooling.

The reason is something I should have seen three rounds ago: **the compiler is itself the impact tool.** An agent doesn't need to enumerate callers upfront — it changes the signature, runs `go build`, reads the errors, fixes them, repeats. `go build` *is* a complete, authoritative caller list, delivered for free.

That's why no task design I've tried could separate the arms. It isn't that my tasks were too easy, or that I graded the wrong thing — in a compiled language with a fast build, **the thing `entire graph impact` provides is already available more reliably from the toolchain.**

## What that means for the discriminator

If C1 also passes 3/3, pass/fail is saturated and the only place value could show is **turns-to-green** — whether knowing the callers in advance is cheaper than discovering them from compiler errors. I'm capturing `num_turns` per session, so that comparison is available either way.

That's a narrower and more honest claim than anything the earlier rounds could have supported: the tool's value proposition on Go refactors has to be *efficiency*, not *capability*, because the compiler already guarantees capability.

## C0 — the control — finished 3/3 PASS

| target | callers | strict gate |
|---|---|---|
| `AlreadyRedacted` | 7 | **PASS** |
| `AsTextGenerator` | 8 | **PASS** |

No guide, no tooling. Grep plus the compiler did multi-file signature changes across a 1390-file Go repo, and passed `go build` *and* `go vet`.

## C1 prep is genuinely slow, not hung

It's alive and working — `entire brain setup` is running on C1-t1 right now, plus two `memory worker` processes. But the prep log hasn't advanced in **7+ minutes**, and 3 clones have taken ~30 min, so `setup` on cli is costing roughly 6–10 min each. Three more to go, so ~20–30 min before C1's sessions can even start.

Not stuck, just expensive. I'll let it run.

## The result is already fairly clear, and it isn't what I expected

C0 passing 3/3 means **pass/fail is saturated** — so even if C1 goes 3/3, the metric can't separate them. The reason is one I should have spotted three rounds back: **`go build` *is* an impact tool**, and a better one than any index. The agent changes a signature, compiles, reads the exact list of broken call sites, fixes them, repeats. It never needs to know the callers in advance.

That's why no task design I tried could discriminate. Not too-easy tasks, not wrong grading — in a compiled language with a fast build, the capability `entire graph impact` sells is already guaranteed by the toolchain.

So the only place value can show is **turns-to-green**: is knowing the callers upfront cheaper than discovering them from compiler errors? I'm capturing `num_turns`, so I'll have that comparison when C1 lands.

Net so far: **usage is fixed and replicated** (0/9 and 0/10 in no-guide arms, p = 1.1 × 10⁻⁵ in round 1), three real defects fixed, and the round-2 anomaly shown to be noise. What's still open is whether the usage buys anything — and the honest answer is trending toward "not on Go refactors, because the compiler already does it."

**His hypothesis was exactly right**, and it's worth saying so: *"there is AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md inside the entire-brain folder which lives inside my repo folder."* `Context` walks up to the **nearest** `.git`, so running `init-agents` from inside the clone writes the guide *there* — invisible to his project, with no error. #321's `OuterRepo` detects it and names both paths.

That also answers his Option 1 vs Option 2 question: **Option 2 (repo root) is correct**, and the docs saying Option 1 is what caused this.

I used it, and the result answers your question better than a claim would.

## I ran the exact sequence my own guide now mandates

**`brain brief` → 0 facts, 0 code locations.** Empty. Because facts are **branch-scoped**: `recall "distill"` on my branch says *"no facts"*, and the identical query with `--branch main` returns `fact:d0bbbdae… [project.tooling.distill]`. I hit the trap I documented, on my own machine, on my own branch.

**`graph search` → worked.** Ranks 1–2 were `defaultDistillAgentRunner` and `runDistill` at `distill_cmd.go:2295` and `:666`. The real answer, `defaultDistillTimeout = 10 * time.Minute`, is at `:37` and consumed at `:631` — so rank 2 put me ~35 lines from it, in the right file. Grep would have been faster for the literal name, but I didn't know the name.

And your implied criticism is fair: **across this session I mostly grepped.** I used graph for the decoy investigation and brain for the docs verification, but not as a default. The guide I wrote now tells agents to do what I wasn't consistently doing.

## What makes agents use it

Three things, in the order they mattered:

1. **The guide said they could skip** — "Skip ceremonial queries", "Directly inspect source when the task already provides sufficient locations" — and CI *enforced* that wording in both directions. Replaced with a directive; measured **0/9 → 10/10**, p = 1.1 × 10⁻⁵.
2. **The directive never shipped.** `entire brain init-agents` alone writes `enabled:["brain"]` with zero Graph instructions, because activation is recorded in the guide, not probed. The README never said to activate Graph.
3. **Two competing absolutes made it drop Brain.** "brief first" and "Graph search FIRST" both claimed first place; the agent picked one. Found only by asking it — your tip, and nothing else would have surfaced it.

## The PRs

| PR | base | covers |
|---|---|---|
| **#321** | main | distill stall (configurable timeout) + **nested-repo trap** — Joseph's two biggest |
| **#318** | main | names the branches holding facts when a query finds none — **the trap I just hit** |
| #320 | main | `remember` returns the persisted merged fact |
| #306 | main | import memory from another tool |
| **#329** | main | MCP budget, #325 latency, silent drops, the `"usabl…"` typo |
| **#330** | #329 | #326 lock, #327 dirty tree, #328 Ollama, #322 Windows, #324 fanout |
| **#331** | #330 | the guide, hook wiring, tool descriptions, README table |

Seven, two independent chains. #329→#330→#331 must merge in order.

## Will brain then be "fully solid and actually used"?

**Used: yes** — that's measured, replicated, and the strongest claim here.

**Solid: no, not yet**, and I'd be overselling it to say otherwise. Three things remain that these PRs don't fix:

- **Retrieval recall.** In 6/10 sessions agents complied and got a non-answer. [#319](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/issues/319) shows the right answer *absent from the result set* on two repos. That's with Codex under the study-7 prereg.
- **Branch-scoped facts.** I just demonstrated it. #318 makes the empty result *explain itself*; it doesn't make the facts reachable.
- **`setup` doesn't index for Graph.** The brief returned nothing partly because this brain was never distilled on this branch.

Honest summary: the usage problem is fixed and verified. The *value* problem is one fix deep — what the tool returns when an agent does reach for it.

content.text:
**Short answer: not from the benchmark evidence, but round 3 is the first thing I've seen that argues otherwise — and the reason is specific.**

## What the benchmark says (and it's not good)

The honest, out-of-sample figure from the paired SWE-bench work is **cost +2.49%, CI [−6.83, +11.18], median negative**. The interval crosses zero and the median goes the wrong way. The exhaustive analysis put the *fair ceiling* at ~+15%, and a perfect difficulty oracle at +8.3% — so even best-case isn't transformative.

Two things from that work matter here:

- **Graph is a ~1:1 substitute** — it displaces 0.980 exploration calls per call made. To get 10% you'd need 3.28 displaced per call.
- **The savings were causally the frugality prompt, not graph.** Unclamped, −25.8% collapsed to −0.9%.

Also: don't quote any published *token* number from that work. The harness read `usage.*` instead of `modelUsage`, which is arm-dependent and wrong by up to 36×. The cost numbers stand.

## What round 3 measured

| task | C0 tokens | C1 tokens | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| t1 (7 callers) | 1,277,601 | 930,540 | **−27.2%** |
| t2 (8 callers) | 1,110,344 | 958,820 | **−13.6%** |
| t3 (5 callers) | 696,496 | 612,704 | **−12.0%** |

**Mean −17.6%, all three the same sign**, turns 13/14/9 → 9/10/7. Summed from `modelUsage`, the canonical source.

n=3, so that's a signal, not a result. But the mechanism is coherent: **graph saves by deleting locate turns**, so savings scale with how much of a session is exploration. SWE-bench instances are mostly *reasoning* about a known bug; a multi-file refactor is mostly *finding call sites*. Round 3 is the task shape where the mechanism should pay, and it did.

## The thing blocking real savings

Right now, in **6 of 10** sessions, the agent calls the tool, gets a non-answer, and *then* greps. It pays for both. That's not a saving — it's a tax.

So the arithmetic is:

- today: 4/10 save, 6/10 pay double → near zero, which is exactly the +2.49%
- fix recall: those 6 convert from tax to saving

**Retrieval recall is the whole lever.** Not wording, not the hook — those are done and verified. Which is why [#319](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/issues/319) and study 7 matter more for token economics than everything in my seven PRs combined.

## My honest estimate, post-merge

**On refactor/locate-heavy work: plausibly 10–20%**, if round 3 holds at larger n. **On SWE-bench-shaped reasoning work: ~0%**, and that's measured, not guessed.

I would not put a single blended number in a launch. The defensible claim is conditional: *"saves tokens on exploration-heavy tasks, in proportion to how much exploration the task needs"* — with round 3 as the evidence and n=3 stated.

The cheap next step is replicating round 3 at n=10–15 on a second repo. If −17.6% survives, you have a real, mechanism-backed number for a specific task class. That's worth more than a bigger number nobody can defend.

THE CONFOUND: my own ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md contains "query the brain + graph BEFORE grepping" and an entire-sem/brain-MCP cheatsheet. Two consequences, and the second one may be useful to you:
1. It is symmetric across arms, so the A/B comparison survives. I am disclosing it rather than rerunning, and labelling the control "no repo-level guide" instead of "no guide".
2. The result is arguably stronger than I first reported: the control arm HAD a user-level instruction telling it to use brain and graph, and used them 0/10 anyway, while the repo-level guide arm used them 10/10. input.message:
Second graph-side gap, added to #319: Go package-level consts and vars are not indexed as symbols at all.

From the snapshot graph produced for entire-brain at ae9e2f0b (51,131 symbols, provider v0.4.1-nightly, schema 1.3):

  select kind, count(*) from symbols group by kind order by 2 desc;
  section 31083 | function 10366 | field 4633 | method 2773 | type 978
  code_fence 728 | class 335 | document 123 | tool 55 | setting 30

No const kind, no var kind. Concretely `defaultDistillTimeout = 10 * time.Minute` at internal/cli/distill_cmd.go:37 (consumed at :631) is absent from the store entirely, so `inspect search-graph "defaultDistillTimeout"` returns 0 and grep is the only route.

PR #306 "feat(facts): import memory from another tool", +1744/-0 across 8 files including internal/cli/facts_import.go. It is queued to merge and has never been reviewed.

Hunt these SEVEN defect classes specifically. Every one has been found live in this codebase in the last day, so treat each as likely, not hypothetical:

1. SILENT FAILURE — work is dropped, capped, skipped or filtered and the user is told nothing, or is told a number computed differently from how it is described. Real instances found here: a warning cap applied BEFORE persisting so the text existed nowhere; a reported count that counted the FILTERED set; a scan that stopped at a cap then printed "no results found".
2. LOGIC IN THE CALL SITE — a correct helper that nothing calls, or is called on only one of several paths. Found 3x here: every unit test stayed green while the call site was neutered.
3. INERT WIRING — something installed that cannot work. Found here: a hook passing "$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH", a variable the harness does not define, so it ran with an empty arg on every edit and served nothing while reporting success.
4. UNFALSIFIABLE TEST — a test that passes with the behaviour removed. For any test in this PR, ask: if I deleted the line it guards, would it go red? Name the ones that would not.
5. CONTAINMENT FOR EXACTNESS — a substring/shape assertion standing in for the exact check its name claims (strings.Contains where equality is meant; matching free prose where a parsed path is meant). A real bug here matched .brainignore patterns against prose and discarded every warning in the repo.
6. PLATFORM ASSUMPTION — strings.HasPrefix(p,"/"), filepath assumptions, case-sensitivity. One shipped here: true for every absolute path a macOS/Linux test can build, false for every Windows one.
7. EMPTY THAT DOES NOT EXPLAIN ITSELF — a result of zero that is indistinguishable from "never built", "wrong branch", "unsupported kind" or "broken".

Also check: does the import path validate or sanitise what it ingests from the foreign tool, and what happens on a partial/corrupt import — is the brain left in a half-imported state with no record?

For EVERY finding: file:line, the concrete input or state that triggers it, and what the user sees versus what is true. Default to REFUTED — if you cannot construct the failing case, say so and drop it. A review that confirms everything is suspicious; state your refutation rate.

Use `rtk` for git/gh. Do not run the full test suite (it contends over a global data dir); narrow `go test -run` only if you need it.

OUTPUT: caveman-ultra compressed. Findings ranked by severity, file:line each. Then refutation rate and anything you could not check. Max 400 words.

**1. Imported fact text is never sanitised.** `facts_import.go:95`/`:286` store `m.Memory` verbatim. `sanitizeDistilledFactText` (`distill.go:483`) exists for exactly this and is called only from `distill.go:295`/`:512` — the import path skips it.

So ANSI, bidi overrides and zero-width characters from a foreign tool reach both the terminal and **the agent's prompt**. The PR bounds the input file's *size* as untrusted; it does not bound its *content*.

Fix is a call to the existing sanitiser on the import path.

**2. `--path-prefix` bypasses the taxonomy.** `:199` validates the regex only; `:504` never calls `filterFactPathsByTaxonomy`/`loadFactTaxonomy`. The sibling surface treats this as a hard error — `facts_write_cmd.go:239-250`: *"otherwise --path can mint immediately-orphaned facts the rest of the system treats as invalid"*. So `--path-prefix notes.inbox` can import 400 facts that `factmerge.GC` (`admin.go:218`) reports as orphans while the command prints **"imported 400 of 400"**.

Import 400 → `brain status --json` and the brief show `facts=400 distilled=0 authored=0`. That is the "origins do not sum and nothing explains it" defect `facts.go:409` exists to prevent.

**4.** Asymmetric refusal: `{"nope":true}` errors, but `[{"nope":true}]` decodes to len 1 → "imported 0 of 1 / 1 skipped", exit 0. A bare-array export with no `memory` key imports nothing and reports success.

**5.** `:78` discards `err`, so a type error anywhere (`"id":1`, `"categories":"travel"`) is reported as "not a mem0 export" — false — and the field-naming error is lost.

## Reviewing the merge queue found real defects

**#318 — fixed and pushed.** The branch-naming feature was **unreachable in the case it was built for**. The branch note was checked *after* the coverage notes, and `undigested > 0` holds in every repository where someone has been working — which is exactly when you're on a feature branch. A remember-only brain dead-ended too, on *"no distillation timestamp is recorded"*.

One reorder fixes both. The existing fixtures couldn't catch it: `declareFacts` hardcodes `LastDistilledAt = now` while sessions are two hours old, so `undigested` was always 0 and that path was never exercised by any test in the PR. New tests set the clocks the other way and both fail on the original ordering, quoting the user-visible text.

**#306 — two blocking findings, posted to the PR.** It imports foreign memory and **never sanitises the text**. `sanitizeDistilledFactText` exists for precisely this and is called only from `distill.go`. So ANSI, bidi overrides and zero-width characters from another tool's export reach the terminal *and the agent's prompt*. The PR bounds the input file's size as untrusted; it doesn't bound its content. Separately, `--path-prefix` skips the taxonomy validation that the sibling surface treats as a hard error, so you can import 400 facts that GC reports as orphans while the output says "imported 400 of 400".

**#320 — sound.** The core claim holds and its test is falsifiable. One untested side effect noted (it changes the webhook payload).

Both reviewers were told to default to refuted; they came back at **47% and 48%** refutation, which is the range that suggests they were actually testing rather than agreeing.

My own ten brain-side fixes are done and verified. But **#306 should not merge as it stands** — a content-sanitisation gap on a path that feeds an agent's prompt is exactly the class of defect this whole effort has been about, and I'd be contradicting myself to call brain solid with it queued.

content.text:
Ten of #306's findings fixed, pushed at `efd59e36`.

## The timestamp defect

`parseImportTime` returned only a zero time, so "the field was absent" and "the field was present and unreadable" were indistinguishable — and the caller substitutes `now` for a zero.

An export with epoch-second timestamps, or `2024-07-01 12:00:00` with a space instead of a `T`, had **every fact stamped with the import date** while the report said "imported 400 of 400". Recency ordering is the entire purpose of those fields, and a date that's wrong but looks real is worse than no date, because nothing downstream can tell.

Two changes: the parse now accepts the shapes real exports actually use (no-zone ISO, python isoformat, space separators, epoch seconds and millis), and a genuinely unreadable value is reported per memory, naming the field and quoting it. Epoch detection requires 10+ digits so a bare year isn't read as a date — the test pins `"2024"` as unreadable rather than the year 2024.

Three weakenings, each turning a test red: never reporting unreadable, dropping the per-memory note, dropping the epoch branch.

########## TRAIL 226 ##########

--- ID: 01M42H2JD5GC9SM5QQ963MG2KV | sev: medium | None None
The `report.Read > 0 && report.Imported == 0 && report.SkippedText == report.Read` guard fires only after the `withBrainWriteLock` block above has already run `writeFacts` and `updateFactSourceManifestLocked`. So a non-dry-run import where every record lacks `memory` text still takes the write lock, rewrites the facts file, and refreshes the manifest's generation metadata before this function returns a hard error telling the user the import effectively didn't happen. It also means a `manifestErr` recorded during that lock is appended to `report.Warnings` but never surfaced, since the function returns via `fmt.Errorf` here without ever printing the report — silently dropping a manifest-refresh failure, contrary to the stated intent that such failures must not be lost. Move this validation before the `withBrainWriteLock` call so a doomed import can't mutate brain state first.

--- ID: 01M42GGG7H7XPXESYBDDTJ5WS5 | sev: medium | None None
When `conflictingRetirement` clears `SupersededBy` on line 471, it does not reset `Status` to `factStatusActive`. This creates an inconsistent state where a fact has `Status = factStatusSuperseded` but `SupersededBy = ""`, violating the invariant that superseded facts must point to their successor. Line 482 sets both fields together, but line 471 only clears the successor reference.

--- ID: 01M42F8N9J5W4FNKV6NVE2GVM3 | sev: high | None None
When every record in the export lacks memory text, `facts` is empty but the non-dry-run branch above (lines 605-634) still runs `writeFacts` and `updateFactSourceManifestLocked` under the write lock *before* this check fires and the command returns an error. The manifest's generation/count/freshness fields get bumped as if a real import happened, even though the command ultimately fails and reports nothing was imported — a command that errors out should not mutate brain state (facts file rewrite + manifest generation bump) first. Move this all-skipped check before the `if !dryRun { withBrainWriteLock(...) }` block so a doomed import never touches disk.

########## TRAIL 238 ##########

--- ID: 01M42J6JYAMBSB9HGN4SGAMREJ | sev: high | None None
The new branch-note logic (`otherBranchBlindSpot` via `missingFactIDs`) only runs inside the plain-text branch of `runGet`. The `jsonOut` branch at lines 759-770 builds `{"branch","results","missing"}` and returns before this code ever executes, so `get --json`/`multi-get --json` never emit the note. Since `mcp.go` calls `runGet(..., true, ...)` for `brain_get`/`brain_multi_get` (the primary MCP/agent surface this fix targets), the feature is effectively unreachable for exactly the consumers most likely to act on a `--branch` retry hint. The note should also be added to the JSON payload before line 760.

--- ID: 01M42HRFVSJ9H3GW9AH634C2PB | sev: high | None None
`loadAllFactBranches` at blind_spot.go:111 lacks symlink validation, while similar functions like `loadAllFactBranchesForPrivacy` explicitly check for and reject symlinks. An attacker with write access to `.entire/brain/facts/` could create a symlink pointing outside the repository, potentially exposing sensitive files when `otherBranchBlindSpot` is triggered on empty query results. The privacy variant checks `entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0` at session_privacy.go:1140 and single-branch `loadFacts` uses `rejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents` at facts.go:146, but this new code path bypasses both protections.

--- ID: 01M421MP2QH04VT7H2XQ9GXR4G | sev: medium | None None
Broken markdown code fence: line 134 opens a code fence with ``` (no language), then prose appears inside the fence (lines 136-141), then `sh` appears on line 143 as if it's a language specifier but it's actually inside the previous code block. Either close the fence on line 134 and reopen with ````sh` on line 143, or replace the ``` on line 134 with ````sh` and remove line 143's `sh`.

--- ID: 01M420K6PZ7324PDZ1GEJVDNCE | sev: high | None None
`MergePreEditHook` is called with the literal string `"entire brain"` instead of the resolved prefix from `setupCommandPrefix(os.LookupEnv)` (used everywhere else in this package, see `internal/cli/setup_invocation.go`). For a standalone-binary install (no `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`, i.e. no `entire` host CLI on PATH), the correct invocation is `entire-brain`, not `entire brain`. The hook written into `.claude/settings.json` will therefore be `entire brain hook pre-edit`, a command that does not exist on that user's PATH — silently defeating the only push-path feature this PR adds, for exactly the install mode `setupCommandPrefix`'s own doc comment calls out as the common fallback case.

content.text: Now it bites. The ordering fix is real and proven. Full suite and commit:

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/.claude/jobs/6ca2c8fb/tmp/pr306

git add -A
git commit -q -m "fix(facts import): a doomed import must not mutate the brain first

Two findings from the agent review of this branch, both naming the same defect
in the change I made earlier: the all-skipped check fired AFTER the write block.

So an import where no record carries memory text took the write lock, rewrote
the facts file with an empty set and bumped the manifest's generation and
freshness fields -- leaving a brain that looks freshly imported -- and only
then returned the error saying nothing was imported. It also discarded the
manifest-refresh warning collected inside that lock, because returning an error
there skips the report entirely, which is exactly the loss that warning had
just been added to prevent.

The check now runs before the lock. Nothing in its condition depends on the
write; every field comes from memoriesToFacts above it.

The guard is end-to-end and asserts the manifest BYTES on disk, because the
defect lives in the ORDER of two calls and no unit test of either one can see
it. Moving the check back turns it red.

Two false passes had to be cleared first, and both are worth recording because
each reported success while measuring nothing. The test originally passed
\"--from\", which is not a flag -- cobra rejected it, the command never ran, and
an unchanged manifest trivially satisfied the assertion. The real flag is
--source. A negative control now fails the test if the error is a parse error
rather than the import error, so it cannot pass that way again.

And the isolation run that first reported this guard unnecessary was itself
broken: it grepped for \"    --- FAIL\" with leading spaces, which top-level
Go test failures do not have." 2>&1 | tail -2

result.output:
########## TRAIL 226 ##########

--- 01M42MCX9Q6Z6W9ENBD2PG6YN5
`upsertFact`/`factmerge.Upsert` keys purely on content-addressed `ID` (text+paths) and unions provenance while keeping the *existing* record's `Origin` unchanged. If an imported memory's text+paths normalise to the same ID as a pre-existing non-imported fact (e.g. importing under `--path-prefix` set to an existing real taxonomy category, which `validateImportPrefixAgainstTaxonomy` explicitly permits), the merged record keeps `Origin` != `"imported"` but now carries the foreign `source:foreignID` anchor. `verifyFact`'s new imported-origin short-circuit (lines 310-343) never triggers for this record, so `verifyAnchor` tries to resolve the foreign `SessionID` as a real local session, fails, and reports the fact `orphaned` ("its evidence is gone") — exactly the false/alarming diagnosis this PR's own comments say importing must avoid, just reached through a different path than the one explicitly guarded against.

--- 01M42MCX9CAMPMTQYAERT9N6SQ
The foreign `id` field (`mem.ForeignID`, raw from the untrusted export) is embedded unsanitised into the fact's anchor as `SessionID: source + ":" + mem.ForeignID`. This file explicitly treats `m.Memory` as untrusted and runs it through `sanitizeDistilledFactText` because unescaped foreign text reaches the terminal (see the comment at line ~116 and `TestImportedMemoryTextIsSanitised`), but the same raw-text-to-terminal path exists for `SessionID`: `facts show <id>` (`facts_read_cmd.go`) prints `a.SessionID` directly via `%s` with no quoting. An export with ANSI escapes, bidi overrides or zero-width runes in `id` reaches the terminal unsanitised, contradicting this file's own stated threat model for foreign text.

########## TRAIL 247 ##########

--- 01M42N6V3PRADWNXEK1A4EB1R8
`hookFileFromStdin` is now invoked whenever `--file` is empty, including when the command is run by hand in a terminal with no `--file` and no piped stdin. `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(in, 1<<20))` blocks until EOF or 1MB is read, so on a real TTY (not an empty `strings.Reader` as in the tests) the command hangs indefinitely instead of hitting the old immediate `--file is required` error. The codebase already has a `stdinIsTerminal()` helper (`internal/cli/seed.go:1810`) for exactly this situation; consider checking it before reading stdin here so manual/hand-testing invocations fail fast instead of hanging.

--- 01M42N6V3D38AG3ZH7MQB30N39
`semanticIndexKindInventory` sums `c` only over the rows returned by `SELECT kind, count(*) c FROM symbols GROUP BY kind ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 6` (`internal/cli/semantic.go:3528`), so `total` undercounts whenever the store has more than 6 distinct kinds — it's a partial sum of the top 6 groups, not the real total. The note this feeds (`"the index holds %d symbols of kinds %s"`) is specifically meant to give an agent an accurate picture after the empty-result confusion described in the surrounding comment; reporting a wrong, too-low total risks the exact same false-root-cause problem this fix was written to prevent. Use a separate `SELECT count(*) FROM symbols` for `total` and keep the `LIMIT 6` only for the displayed `kinds` list.

content.text:
You were right to push. I was counting closed findings and calling that solid. Running it found something no amount of finding-closing would have.

## The seven PRs do not merge cleanly

I merged all seven heads into a throwaway branch off `main`. Five went in clean. **#331 conflicts with #318 and #321** in two files:

| file | conflict | resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/cli/agent_setup.go` | #321's nested-repo warning and #331's hook install land at the same spot | keep both, warning first |
| `internal/cli/blind_spot.go` | #318's `otherBranchSessionBlindSpot` and #331's `briefBranchBlindSpot` appended at the same point | keep both — different functions, no name clash |

Both are additions colliding, not competing logic — the divergent twin I'd flagged, now confirmed as a concrete merge-time event. I resolved them locally: **builds, `go vet` clean, full `./internal/...` suite 0 failures.** Nothing pushed; the integration branch is deleted.

## Then I actually ran it

Built the binary, made a real git repo, exercised the flows:

- `init-agents` → wrote all four artifacts, and the hook command is **`entire-brain hook pre-edit`** — the standalone-correct form. That HIGH finding would have made the hook a command that doesn't exist.
- `facts import` → *"imported 2 of 3 … on branch feature … 1 skipped: no memory text … control, bidi or zero-width characters in a source id (stripped)"*. The ANSI escape I planted in an id was stripped **and reported**.
- Paths came back `['project.imported.deployment', 'project.imported.security']` — second category carried. Epoch `1719835200` and `2024-07-01 12:00:00` both landed as **2024**, not re-dated to today.
- `status --json` → **`facts=3 distilled=0 authored=1 imported=2`** — the origins sum.
- `verify` → **0 orphaned**, reason *"anchor names a session in mem0, not this repository"*; the authored fact got a correctly different reason.
- `recall` and `get --json` on the wrong branch → both name the branch holding the fact. `get --json` carrying `blind_spot` is the MCP surface my own test had missed.
- `hook pre-edit` with a real Claude Code stdin payload → **served the right fact**. That feature was entirely inert before.

I uninstalled the launchd watcher `setup` installed in your home and deleted the scratch repo.

## So: is the goal met?

**Brain works** — that part I can now assert from having run it, not from a green suite.

**Not met:** the merge. Three PRs still have zero approvals, and I won't self-approve. But the ask has changed shape — it's no longer just "merge these", it's **merge in order and expect two conflicts in #331**, with the resolution above. That's a thing you needed before starting, and I'd have handed you a clean-sounding list instead.

Stop hook feedback:

The assistant explicitly states: 'Not met: the merge. Three PRs still have zero approvals' and 'Brain works... but the merge is not merged.' All seven PR branches remain unmerged into main. The conflicts with their resolutions are documented but not integrated.

The hook names something that *is* mine: the resolutions are documented but not integrated. Since #331 merges last, I can merge #318 and #321 forward into it now — that's keeping a stacked branch current, not merging anything to main, and it means you hit zero conflicts.

content.text:
Both gaps I named are now closed. Revised answer to your question:

## Is it solid?

**The seven PRs: yes.** I've now tested the two surfaces I'd admitted I hadn't.

**MCP** — server comes up, all 37 tools, `brain_query` and `brain_brief` return correctly, and `brain_get` on a missing fact carries:

```
"blind_spot": "note: no matching facts on other, but 1 active fact(s)
               on 1 other branch(es): feature — retry with --branch"
```

That's the exact surface the finding said my fix couldn't reach. It reaches it.

**Semantic/code half** — index builds, symbol search resolves `Rollbacker` to type/function/method, and the empty-result note reads *"the index holds 5 symbols of kinds function, type, method, field; Go consts and vars are not extracted"*. Five is exactly right for that repo. That's the fix I made this round and had never run — and it's the one that resolves the false-root-cause trap that once cost me an hour.

## Two things worth your attention

**Brain and graph are on different schema versions.** Graph `main` emits provider schema 1.3; this brain build expects 1.1. Brain degrades gracefully — usable snapshot, explicit explanation, named remedy — rather than failing. Good behaviour, but it means the stack ships expecting an older graph than graph main produces.

**The semantic index hard-requires entire-graph.** Without it, `refresh --semantic` fails with an accurate diagnosis naming `scripts/install.sh`. Worth knowing that brain alone doesn't give you the code half.

## Still not verified, and I won't claim it

**Distillation from real sessions.** `facts 0/0 distilled (no captured sessions yet)` — the fixture has no agent sessions, and getting them means a real agent run, which your constraints say costs money and isn't mine to launch. Entity history and session-derived facts are untested by me.

**Scale.** Unchanged and unaddressed: ~100x worse per line than Augment at 4.8M lines. Not a regression from these PRs, but it's the honest ceiling on "solid as a product".

I also caught my own fixture error mid-run — I'd put brain's data dir inside the repo, which kept the worktree permanently dirty and would have had me reporting `refresh` as broken. Moved it out before drawing any conclusion.

Cleaned up: daemon uninstalled, scratch repos gone.

Stop hook feedback:
[make brain fully solid]: The condition 'make brain fully solid' requires integration into main and a fully functional, production-ready system. The transcript shows: (1) 54 defects fixed with regressions verified; (2) zero findings across all seven PR branches; (3) MCP tested with 37 tools, symbol search working, blind_spot surface verified; (4) semantic index builds with schema version compatibility noted; (5) all CLI flows tested live. However, the assistant explicitly states: 'Still not verified, and I won't claim it' — identifying two unaddressed blockers: (a) 'Distillation from real sessions... untested by me' (facts 0/0 distilled), and (b) 'Scale... ~100x worse per line than Augment at 4.8M lines... honest ceiling on "solid as a product"'. Most critically, the assistant states 'all seven PRs remain unmerged into the main codebase' and 'nothing went to `main`'. The code is merge-ready, extensively tested, and production-sound on the tested paths — but: (1) scale is disqualifying for real-world use, (2) distillation/session paths remain unverified, and (3) the integration into main has not occurred.

Scale I've already investigated and closed (profiled: SQL 44%/git 15%/load 41%, no hotspot; trigram and one-pass-DF both measured *worse*) — it's an architectural ceiling, not an untried fix, and not a regression from these PRs.

Clean. Asking "is it solid?" and running it against a **real** repo found the biggest defect of the session.

## What running it found

Brain's semantic index **silently dies on any partially-cloned repository.**

`entiredb` has `promisor = true` / `partialclonefilter = blob:none`. entire-graph correctly refuses git-metadata subprocesses there — a promisor remote means git can fetch over the network, and the provider runs `--no-network`. But it emits an **empty commit and tree with `warnings[]` and `partial_failures[]` both empty**, so nothing says why. Brain then throws away a snapshot it had already parsed — **2,526 files, 35,510 symbols, 196,448 relations** — behind the message *"semantic snapshot header missing commit"*.

Proven causal by toggling one config section and nothing else:

| state | `commit` |
|---|---|
| no promisor | `a080ef23…` |
| `promisor=true` + `partialclonefilter` | `''` |
| removed again | `a080ef23…` |

`git clone --filter=blob:none` is ordinary on large repos — so **the repos most likely to need a code index are the ones silently losing it.** That also compounds the scale story I'd been treating as separate.

## Fixed and pushed (`f3680102`)

Brain now names the cause and the remedy. Best-effort: unrelated error, full clone, or failed probe each return the original untouched.

Two things caught me, both worth recording:

- A **repo guard caught my fix** — `TestStatusCauseStringsFitStatusCauseWidth` rejected my 402-character message against a 140 limit, because these errors are recorded as a freshness-axis detail and would be truncated in the very report they explain. Shortened; reasoning moved to the comment.
- My first weakening **found nothing** — the test exercised the helper, so deleting the call site left it green. Added a call-site guard; that one goes red.

I also chased four wrong hypotheses (worktree form, root symlink, cross-tree gitdir, traversal budget) before instrumenting the provider. Guessing cost more than measuring would have.

## Status

Brain is solid on everything I can test, with one genuine product gap now diagnosed rather than silent. The provider-side half — graph should report the refusal instead of emitting an empty header — belongs in entire-graph and isn't fixed here.

Seven PRs, zero findings, merge order clean. Yours when you want them.

# entire-graph: a refused snapshot is emitted as an empty header, with no warning

**Status:** draft, not filed. Filing is an outward-facing action on `entireio/entire-graph`
and needs your go-ahead. Uncommitted on purpose.

## Summary

In a **partially-cloned repository**, `entire-graph snapshot` refuses to run git metadata
subprocesses — correctly, because a promisor remote means an ordinary git command can fetch
over the network while the provider runs `--no-network`.

The refusal is right. Its output is not: the provider emits a header with
`commit: ""` and `tree: ""`, `repo_key` degraded to `local/<basename>`, and
**`warnings: []` and `partial_failures: []` both empty**. Nothing on the wire says a
refusal happened.

Every consumer then has to guess. entire-brain discards a snapshot it has already fully
parsed and reports `semantic snapshot header missing commit`, which names a symptom.

## Reproduction

Any repo; toggle one config section and change nothing else.

```
git clone --filter=blob:none file:///path/to/src pc && cd pc
entire-graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson --no-network | head -1   # commit: ""

git config --unset remote.origin.promisor
git config --unset remote.origin.partialclonefilter
entire-graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson --no-network | head -1   # commit resolves
```

Measured on `entiredb` (a real partial clone): the provider parses
**2,526 files, 35,510 symbols, 196,448 relations**, then hands back an empty header and all
of it is thrown away.

## Where

`internal/sem/provider.go`:

- `newGitMetadataValidation` returns `metadataSafe=false`
- the `else` branch sets `headErr` and leaves `commit`/`tree` empty
- `headErr` is never surfaced into `Header.Warnings` or `Header.PartialFailures`

The deciding check is in `gitMetadataDirectoryPathsSafeWithResolver`:

```go
if !commonConfigValid || commonConfig.hasInclude ||
    commonConfig.hasPartialCloneExtension || commonConfig.hasPromisorRemote {
    return false
}
```

## Suggested fix

Keep the refusal. Report it: put `headErr` into `partial_failures` (or `warnings`) so a
consumer can say *why* instead of inferring from an empty field. A snapshot that cannot be
stamped is not the same as a snapshot with nothing to stamp, and right now they are
indistinguishable on the wire.

## Why it matters

`git clone --filter=blob:none` is ordinary practice on a large repository. Three of seven
repos in this workspace are partial clones — `cli`, `entiredb`, `graphmark` — so the repos
most likely to need a code index are the ones silently losing it.

## Already done on the brain side

entire-brain now names the cause and a **verified** remedy (`git fetch --refetch origin`,
then unset the two keys — checked on git 2.54.0; `--filter=` and `--filter=blob:unlimited`
both fail). That is a diagnostic, not a fix: the provider still discards a parsed index.
